front.title: Multicast Delivery and Endpoint Discovery for Media over QUIC

abstract.t: This document specifies multicast delivery mechanisms and catalog-based endpoint discovery for Media over QUIC (MoQ). It defines how MoQ sessions integrate with IP multicast (SSM, ASM), Automatic Multicast Tunneling (AMT), and TreeDN for scalable live streaming. The specification includes a multicast catalog extension for endpoint discovery and multi-path delivery across TV, mobile, and browser platforms. All multicast media delivery uses MPEG Media Transport Protocol (MMTP) packets, the same packet format that MoQ objects carry on QUIC streams. A manifest-based content-authentication profile protects multicast delivery with signed manifest records that travel in band beside those packets.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Unicast delivery, including Media over QUIC (MoQ) , replicates a stream per receiver; IP multicast replicates it in the network.
This document specifies how MoQ integrates with IP multicast to combine the scalability of multicast with the reliability and signaling of QUIC:

ol.li: Delivery paths: Platform-specific multicast reception for TV, mobile, and browser clients

Catalog extension: A multicast endpoint discovery mechanism for MoQ catalogs . Endpoints carry mmtp tracks and their repair tracks, and a loc or cmaf track reaches multicast through an mmtp rendition track (Section 4.1).

MMTP wire format: All multicast media delivery uses MMTP packets -- the same packet format that MoQ objects carry on QUIC streams -- and on a protected endpoint signed manifest records travel in band beside them (Section 5).
Multi-path delivery: Combining MoQ unicast and multicast for failover and FEC symbol deduplication

section.t: These mechanisms follow TreeDN , which gives an incremental path to native multicast. A network that supports multicast delivers the stream to its receivers as native SSM. A receiver on a unicast-only network reaches the same stream through an Automatic Multicast Tunneling (AMT) relay that it finds in its own network, from a relay service hostname (Section 3.1), or with DNS Reverse IP AMT Discovery (DRIAD) . Section 4.2.1 describes how a catalog signals both. Each network can therefore turn on multicast when it is ready. Until then, its receivers that have UDP socket access (Section 3) use AMT, and the others stay on MoQ unicast. An AMT relay can replicate packets in router forwarding hardware or in a kernel data plane, so relay fan-out does not cost a server per receiver.

section.name: Multicast as Supplement to MoQ Unicast
section.t: Multicast delivery as defined in this document is a supplement to MoQ/QUIC unicast. Subscribers MUST establish a MoQ session first to receive the catalog, negotiate parameters, and receive initial media. Multicast MAY then be used as an additional delivery path for ongoing media data. This ensures that codec configuration is available before multicast reception begins.

Exception: MMTP-packaged streams delivered via ATSC 3.0 broadcast or native SSM MAY operate as unidirectional data streams without a MoQ session. MMTP carries per-packet routing (packet_id), timing (timestamp), sequencing (Packet Sequence Number), and FEC framing (FEC Type, FEC payload IDs) natively, and its signaling messages identify the Assets in band: every Asset sent to a multicast endpoint is named by a PA message on its sending entity's packet_id 0 signaling sub-flow, whose MP table locates the Asset by source address, group address, port and packet_id (Section 5). A receiver without the catalog takes the FEC configuration from the AL-FEC message ( Section 8.3) when the flow carries one. A receiver that holds the catalog takes both from the catalog, which remains authoritative for media and FEC parameters (Section 4.1; the FEC instance configuration of Section 10 of ). A catalog-provided service name or relay address is only a discovery input; it is not proof that an upstream is reachable or healthy. ATSC 3.0 and ARIB STD-B60 receivers consume MMTP over SSM as their native delivery path.

section.name: Relation to Other Documents
section.t: The FEC that this document applies on multicast paths is specified by four companion documents. defines the scheme-independent FEC mechanism for MoQ and the FEC instance configuration that a catalog carries; specifies the Reed-Solomon scheme, which is mandatory to implement, and the optional RaptorQ scheme; defines the catalog encoding of that configuration, including the fec-repair packaging value and the per-instance fields over which params_hash () is defined; and defines FEC on multicast delivery paths, including repair-only endpoints, the receiver repair policy and block classification. defines the MMTP packaging that multicast endpoints carry, and the part of that FEC that is specific to MMTP packets: the "iso-ssbg1-v1" block profile, the Source FEC Payload ID and the keyframe overlay. The -01 revision of this document cited that material as .

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
SSM: Source-Specific Multicast
AMT: Automatic Multicast Tunneling
DRIAD: DNS Reverse IP AMT Discovery
TreeDN: Tree-based Content Delivery Network

Service hostname: A stable DNS name identifying an upstream MoQ relay or AMT relay service. It is the receiver's connection identity; the A and AAAA records returned for it are candidate addresses, not stable endpoint identities.

Protocol health: Successful completion of the protocol-specific handshake and capability checks required before a receiver selects an upstream. A DNS response, a routable address, or a transport handshake alone is not protocol health.
MMTP: MMT Protocol -- the packet layer of MPEG Media Transport ( Clause 9; Section 3).

MMT sending entity: The entity that packetizes media into MMTP packets and sends them on one or more multicast endpoints. It is the scope over which Section 4.1 assigns each packetId value to exactly one MMTP packet sub-flow, and it serves exactly one MoQ namespace (Section 4.1).

section.name: Delivery Paths
section.t: MoQ content can reach receivers via multiple delivery paths depending on platform capabilities:

tr.td: SSM direct via OS multicast API

section.t: Both native SSM and AMT tunneling require UDP socket access. MoQ/WebTransport is the fallback that every client supports and requires no special platform capabilities.
Broadcast receivers (ATSC 3.0, ARIB STD-B60) consume MMTP streams natively over RF tuner hardware. MoQ integration occurs at the gateway/head-end level via TreeDN and AMT / DRIAD .

Several transports can be available for a given stream. When more than one delivery path is available, receivers SHOULD prefer, in order: tuner-based broadcast reception (where tuner hardware exists), native SSM, AMT tunneling, and finally MoQ/QUIC unicast. Local policy MAY override this order. Within tuner-based reception, receivers prefer Single Frequency Network (SFN) diversity reception, where deployed, over single-transmitter reception.

section.name: Receiver-Owned DNS Candidate Discovery
section.t: When a receiver is given a service hostname for a MoQ upstream or an AMT relay, it MUST perform discovery from that hostname at connection time. The resolver's A and AAAA answers form a set of candidate addresses. DNS answer order, address reachability, and an address's geographic or topological appearance do not by themselves establish health. Local, anycast, or GeoDNS policy MAY use the resolver to steer the candidate set toward a nearby upstream, but the receiver MUST validate the selected candidate at the protocol layer.

For a MoQ/QUIC upstream, a receiver MUST retain the service hostname for TLS certificate and SNI validation and MUST use a bounded attempt for each candidate. A candidate is healthy only after the QUIC handshake, supported MoQ ALPN negotiation, MoQ session setup, and the capability or catalog check needed by the requested service have succeeded. Receivers MUST bound both the number of concurrent candidate attempts and the duration of each attempt. They SHOULD race a bounded batch of candidates in parallel (or use an equivalent bounded strategy), select the first healthy candidate, and cancel the losing attempts. A candidate that completes QUIC but fails MoQ setup or capability validation MUST NOT prevent another candidate from being tried.

For an AMT relay, a receiver MUST complete the AMT Discovery, Advertisement, Request, and Membership Query exchange when those messages are used, and MUST wait for either the first data packet for the requested source and group or a configured finite post-Membership-Query/Update wait to expire. A receiver MUST NOT wait indefinitely for data: for a source declared sparse or idle by local policy, expiry of that wait MAY permit selection after the control-plane exchange, but the result is control-plane health rather than proof of data-plane delivery. A relay that answers DNS or sends an Advertisement but does not complete the exchange is not healthy. After selection, the receiver MUST use bounded liveness and membership-refresh timers and MUST repeat DNS resolution and the candidate race after tunnel failure or liveness expiry.

Receivers SHOULD honor DNS TTLs for new connection attempts and SHOULD apply only bounded negative caching. An established connection MAY continue after its DNS answer expires, but a reconnect MUST NOT pin a previous address indefinitely. Retries MUST use bounded backoff and MUST cancel stale attempts before starting another bounded batch; at no time may candidate attempts accumulate without a bound. If no candidate becomes healthy, the receiver uses the next permitted delivery path or remains in retry state according to local policy; it MUST NOT declare a path healthy solely because DNS returned an answer.

This procedure applies equally to service hostnames obtained from configuration, an operator provisioning system, or a multicast catalog. An operator provisioning system is a control-plane service that publishes the service hostname, transport metadata, and policy; it is not a substitute for receiver-side protocol health validation. A catalog MUST NOT be interpreted as an authority to bypass that validation. A literal IP address is permitted for an explicitly configured static deployment, but it does not provide DNS locality steering and is not the preferred form for a service that has multiple upstreams.

section.name: Multicast Catalog Extension
section.t: For tracks available via multicast, the MoQ catalog includes a top-level multicast field containing an endpoints array for endpoint discovery.
The catalog is the MSF catalog track, named catalog ( Section 5; Section 13).

section.name: Multicast Endpoint Format
section.t: The multicast field is a root-level extension member of the MSF catalog; the catalog envelope for this suite is described in Section 13. Section 5 permits producers to add fields and requires parsers to ignore fields they do not understand, so a parser that does not support multicast ignores the multicast field.
The multicast field contains an endpoints array listing one or more multicast groups. A single-endpoint deployment uses a one-element array:
Multi-group deployments (e.g., per-quality ABR tiers or separate audio/video groups) use multiple elements:
The multicast object contains the following members:
endpoints (array of objects, REQUIRED): One or more multicast endpoint objects as defined below. The array MUST NOT be empty.
networkSource (array of objects, OPTIONAL): Network delivery configuration applying to all endpoints; see Section 4.2.
auth (object, OPTIONAL): Content authentication configuration for the bc-provenance profile; see Section 7.2.
Endpoint field definitions:
sourceAddress (string, OPTIONAL): SSM source IP address per . Its presence selects SSM and its absence Any-Source Multicast (ASM).
protocol (string, OPTIONAL): "ssm" or "asm", restating that mode. An endpoint where it disagrees with sourceAddress is ignored (see below).
groupAddress (string, REQUIRED): Multicast group address.

ul.li: SSM range: 232.0.0.0/8 (IPv4), ff3x::/32 (IPv6)
ASM range: 224.0.0.0/4 (IPv4), ff00::/8 outside the SSM range ff3x::/32 (IPv6)

section.t: port (integer, REQUIRED): UDP port number.
tracks (array, REQUIRED): Tracks available on this endpoint. Each element is an object with the following fields:

ul.li: name (string, REQUIRED): Track name corresponding to the track identifier used in the MoQ catalog. The name is resolved in the namespace of the catalog track ( Section 5.2.2); an endpoint MUST NOT list a track whose catalog entry declares another namespace. The named track MUST be a track whose packaging is mmtp ( Section 13.1) or a fec-repair track that repairs such a track ( Section 3.3).

packetId (integer, REQUIRED): MMTP packet_id used for packet-level track routing on multicast. Maps directly to the Packet ID field in the MMTP header (Section 3.1 of ). The value is an integer in the range 1..65535. Each value MUST denote exactly one MMTP packet sub-flow across all endpoints of the MMT sending entity (Section 2) for the lifetime of the delivery session, not merely within one (S, G, port) multicast tuple (below); two distinct sub-flows MUST NOT share a value ( Clause 9.2.3). A sub-flow is one sequence of packets with one packet_sequence_number space. An endpoint that carries another endpoint's sub-flow packet for packet therefore carries it under the same value, and every other sub-flow takes a value of its own. The rungs of a ladder never share a value. A catalog track denotes one sub-flow: every endpoint that lists a track carries that track's one sub-flow, under one value. Media that the sending entity packetizes separately for several endpoints, such as audio packetized once per rung, MUST be published as a separate track for each packetization, with its own name, value, fec array and repair tracks, because the copies differ in the bytes that FEC protects ( Section 7.1). packet_id 0 is reserved for the sending entity's MMTP signaling sub-flow ( Section 3.1; Section 5), which arrives on the same tuples as the media; a publisher MUST NOT advertise it for a track.

section.t: bandwidth (integer, REQUIRED on a protected endpoint, RECOMMENDED otherwise): Aggregate bandwidth of this endpoint in bits per second, defined as the sum of the UDP payload bitrates of all tracks carried on the endpoint, including repair tracks, plus the MMTP signaling sub-flow on packet_id 0 (Section 5) where the endpoint carries it; IP/UDP header overhead is excluded. Publishers SHOULD include bandwidth to enable capacity-aware join decisions; on a protected endpoint it is the sender's ceiling for the flow, and a receiver ignores a protected endpoint without it (). Subscribers SHOULD check available network capacity before joining high-bandwidth groups.

auth (object, OPTIONAL when the multicast object has no auth member, REQUIRED otherwise): Content authentication of this endpoint's flow; its presence makes the endpoint a protected flow. Receivers MUST ignore an endpoint that lacks auth when the multicast object carries auth, and an endpoint that carries auth when the multicast object does not (Section 7.2.6). See Section 7.2.
networkSource (array of objects, OPTIONAL): Network delivery configuration for this endpoint; see Section 4.2.

Each (S, G, port) multicast tuple, with S the endpoint's sourceAddress on an SSM endpoint, its auth.senderAddress on a protected ASM endpoint () and absent on an unprotected ASM endpoint, MUST be associated with at most one MoQ namespace and at most one endpoint object. Publishers requiring multiple independent streams MUST use distinct multicast groups or ports. An MMT sending entity (Section 2) serves exactly one MoQ namespace, which is one MMT Package (Section 5); a publisher that serves several namespaces acts as several sending entities, each with its own endpoints, its own packetId assignment and its own packet_id 0 signaling sub-flow. A track listed on an endpoint MUST NOT declare a namespace other than the catalog track's ( Section 5.2.2); a receiver MUST ignore an endpoint that lists one.

Receivers MUST ignore endpoints whose fields are mutually inconsistent -- for example, a protocol of "ssm" with sourceAddress omitted, a sourceAddress present with protocol of "asm", or a groupAddress outside the multicast address space. Receivers MUST likewise ignore an endpoint that lists a track packetId outside the range 1..65535, including 0, the MMTP signaling flow. They MUST also ignore an endpoint that lists a track that the name field does not permit.

This document defines multicast carriage only for mmtp tracks (Section 5). To offer a track packaged as loc or cmaf on multicast, a publisher also publishes an mmtp rendition of the same media: a separate track whose packaging is mmtp, with its own name, packetId, fec array and repair tracks, in the same altGroup as the loc or cmaf track (Section 6.1). The endpoint lists the mmtp rendition track. A receiver that holds the loc or cmaf track over MoQ receives the mmtp rendition track on multicast in its place. The two tracks are separate FEC instances ( Section 5.1), so symbols of one never repair the other, and the multi-path combining of Section 6 applies within the mmtp rendition track only.

Subscribers receiving a catalog with multicast endpoints MAY auto-connect to the multicast group when multicast APIs are available and multicast delivery is preferred (UDP socket access, native or AMT). Multicast joins create IGMP/MLD state on intermediate routers; subscribers SHOULD only join when multicast provides a concrete benefit over unicast.

Joining an SSM endpoint requires source-specific group membership signaling: receivers MUST use IGMPv3 (IPv4) or MLDv2 (IPv6) to convey (S,G) joins. Earlier protocol versions (IGMPv2/MLDv1) cannot express source-specific joins; if the receiver's network segment operates at an earlier version (for example, due to an IGMPv2 querier or snooping switch on the segment), SSM joins fail silently. Receivers SHOULD detect the absence of multicast data following a join and fall back to MoQ/QUIC unicast (Section 6).

During multicast join (which may take 1-3 seconds for IGMP/MLD), subscribers SHOULD continue receiving via MoQ/QUIC. Once multicast data arrives, subscribers switch to the multicast path. Section 6.3 describes how they then pause or end the unicast subscriptions that the multicast path replaces. What a subscriber receives over MoQ/QUIC for a consumer that has not yet admitted a datagram of a protected flow is outside the profile of : the MoQ session protects it, and the receiver MAY verify it against the records of a manifestTrack (); the profile governs a consumer from its first admitted datagram (step 2 of ), at which the receiver discards what the consumer still holds of the flow's tracks that it did not admit.
If multicast reception fails or degrades, subscribers fall back to MoQ/QUIC unicast per Section 6.

Receivers SHOULD implement hysteresis to prevent flapping between multicast and unicast paths. Switch away from multicast after sustained loss or consecutive FEC block failures; switch back only after multicast reception is stable for a sufficient period. Specific thresholds are implementation-defined and configurable.

section.name: Network Source Types
section.t: The networkSource field is an array of network-source objects describing how subscribers can reach the multicast stream when native IP multicast routing is not available. It MAY appear at the multicast level (applying to all endpoints) or on individual endpoints; a single source is expressed as a one-element array.
Each network-source object contains:
type (string, REQUIRED): Delivery technology identifier.
Defined types:

section.name: AMT (Automatic Multicast Tunneling)
section.t: relay (string, OPTIONAL): AMT relay service name. With dns, it MUST be a hostname whose A and AAAA answers are candidate addresses. With manual, it MUST be the literal address of the explicitly configured relay. It MUST be omitted with driad, because DRIAD supplies the relay candidates. A literal address does not provide DNS locality steering.

port (integer, OPTIONAL): UDP port on which the relay named by the relay field accepts requests. When absent, the AMT port (2268, Section 7.2) is used. A value other than 2268 departs from Sections 5.1.1 and 5.1.3 and works only with gateways and relays configured for it. The field never applies to a relay found by DRIAD, whose AMTRELAY record carries no port ( Section 4.2).
discovery (string, OPTIONAL): AMT relay discovery method.

ul.li: "dns": Resolve the relay service hostname to A and AAAA candidates and validate each candidate with the AMT protocol (Section 3.1). This is the RECOMMENDED method when a relay service hostname is available.

"driad": DNS Reverse IP AMT Discovery per . Subscribers query the source IP's reverse DNS for AMT relay records; relay MUST be omitted. Each discovered relay is still a candidate and MUST be validated with the AMT protocol before selection.
"manual": Relay address is provided in the relay field. This is intended for explicitly configured static deployments.

section.t: For dns, subscribers MUST resolve the hostname at each connection and reconnect attempt, bound both the number and duration of AMT validation attempts, and race a bounded batch for the returned A and AAAA candidates. The receiver MUST wait for either first (S,G) data or the configured finite post-Membership-Query/Update wait. It MUST select only a candidate that completes the AMT control-plane exchange; for a sparse or idle source, selection after the wait expires records control-plane health without claiming data-plane proof. DNS answer order is not a health signal.

When cancelling a losing AMT attempt that has reached the Query/Update state, the receiver MUST send a Membership Update carrying the IGMP/MLD leave (withdrawal) for the requested (S,G) Section 5.1.5, then close that candidate's socket. An attempt that has not reached that state is cancelled by closing its socket; a failed cancellation is bounded and MUST NOT keep the candidate attempt alive.
Subscribers SHOULD look for a relay in this order, which keeps the preference of Section 3.1.2 for a relay in the subscriber's own network:

ol.li: Look for a relay in the subscriber's own network, with DNS-based Service Discovery (DNS-SD) for _amt._udp and then through the AMT anycast addresses of Section 7.
Use receiver-owned DNS candidate discovery when discovery is "dns", or when discovery is omitted and relay is a hostname.
Use DRIAD discovery on the SSM source IP when discovery is "driad", or when both discovery and relay are omitted and the source IP has DRIAD records.
Use a literal relay directly when discovery is "manual", or when discovery is omitted and relay is a literal under an explicitly permitted static-deployment policy.

section.t: The discovery and relay fields select at most one of steps 2 to 4 for an endpoint. A relay named by the relay field or found by DRIAD is one that the sender knows, and is not necessarily near the subscriber ( Section 3.1.1). A local relay keeps more of the path on native multicast. Every relay found in steps 1 to 4 is a candidate that the subscriber validates with the AMT protocol before selection (Section 3.1). DRIAD requires AMTRELAY (TYPE260) reverse DNS records on the source IP. Publishers without reverse DNS control SHOULD provide a stable relay service hostname. requires a gateway to carry the ECN field through decapsulation per and Section 6.1.4, which recommends the same support in a relay.

section.name: ATSC 3.0 (Broadcast Television)
section.t: frequency (integer, REQUIRED): RF center frequency in kHz.
plpId (integer, OPTIONAL): Physical Layer Pipe ID (). Defaults to 0.
serviceId (integer, OPTIONAL): Service ID within the broadcast multiplex ().

slsUri (string, OPTIONAL): URI for Service Layer Signaling (SLS) bootstrap. Enables receivers joining via IP (not RF) to acquire the full ATSC 3.0 SLS of an MMTP service, its MP table included ( Section 7.2).
Receivers with ATSC 3.0 tuner hardware can receive the stream directly over RF. MoQ subscribers without tuner hardware ignore this networkSource type.

section.name: Multiple Network Sources
section.t: When a stream is available via multiple delivery technologies, the networkSource array lists one element per technology:
Subscribers select the highest-priority available source per the transport hierarchy defined in Section 3.

section.name: Multicast Packet Format
section.t: All multicast delivery uses MMTP packets. Each UDP datagram, other than a manifest record on a protected endpoint (), carries one MMTP packet -- the same packet format that MoQ objects carry on QUIC streams. MMTP provides track routing (packet_id), send timestamps, sequencing (packet_sequence_number), FEC framing (FEC Type and the Source/Repair FEC Payload IDs) and random access signaling (RAP flag) in its packet header, and fragmentation (FI) in the MPU-mode payload header ( Sections 3.1 and 4.2). For a MoQ receiver, FEC configuration (the FEC instance configuration of Section 10 of , and the scheme parameters that a block FEC scheme derives from it, Sections 5.2 and 6.1 of ) comes from the catalog ( Section 4); a receiver without the catalog relies on the in-band signaling below.

Frame-sized LOC or CMAF objects exceed a UDP datagram, while the MMTP MPU-mode payload format fragments media into MTU-sized packets ( Clause 9.3.2; Section 5.2). Multicast carriage therefore uses MMTP: an endpoint lists only mmtp tracks and their repair tracks, and a loc or cmaf track reaches multicast through an mmtp rendition track (Section 4.1).
No additional multicast framing, encapsulation, or header format is needed. The MMTP packet format is defined in Clause 9.2, as profiled in Section 3.1.
This design means the same MMTP packet can be delivered via three transports without modification:

tr.td: MMTP packet as MoQ stream object
MMTP packet as multicast QUIC DATAGRAM object

section.t: Receivers on multicast demultiplex packets using the MMTP packet_id field, which maps to the packetId assigned in the multicast catalog endpoint (Section 4.1). On a protected endpoint a receiver splits off the manifest records by their first four octets before it reads packet_id (). A receiver MUST NOT deliver to any media or repair decoder a packet whose packet_id is not advertised for a track, for the (S, G, port) multicast tuple (Section 4.1) on which the packet arrived, S being the packet's source address as this section matches it, by an endpoint that the receiver has not ignored under Section 4.1. Packets of the MMTP signaling flow (packet_id 0) are handled per Section 3.1. FEC source and repair packets are distinguished by the MMTP FEC Type field ( Section 3.1).

A publisher MUST identify in band the Assets of every MMTP packet flow that it sends to a multicast endpoint, whether a receiver obtains the flow over native SSM or ASM or through an AMT relay (Section 4.2.1). It does so with one MMTP signaling sub-flow per MMT sending entity (Section 2): a single sequence of packets on packet_id 0, with one packet_sequence_number space, that every endpoint listing a track other than a fec-repair track carries packet for packet, as Section 4.1 requires of any sub-flow carried on several endpoints ( Clause 9.2.3). All endpoints of the sending entity carry one Package. The sub-flow carries a PA message (message_id 0x0000; Clause 10.3.2, Table 21), in the signaling message mode of Section 3.1, with the tables that Clause 10.3.1 requires of a PA message, among them a PA table (Clause 10.3.7, Table 26) and the complete MP table of the Package (table_id 0x20, Clause 10.3.9, Table 29), never a subset. The MP table MUST describe as an Asset each track, other than a fec-repair track ( Section 3.3), that any endpoint of the sending entity lists, and MUST locate it at each endpoint that carries it, and at no other, by an MMT_general_location_info of location_type 0x01 (IPv4) or 0x02 (IPv6) that gives the endpoint's group address and port, the track's packetId, and, as ipv4_src_addr or ipv6_src_addr, the address from which the sending entity transmits that endpoint's flow, which is the source address of its IP packets ( Clause 10.6.1). On an SSM endpoint that address equals the endpoint's sourceAddress (Section 4.1); an ASM endpoint, whose catalog entry has no sourceAddress, still carries the sending entity's own address there. A receiver matches a location by destination address, destination port, packet_id and source address: on an SSM endpoint the source address is the endpoint's sourceAddress, and on an ASM endpoint it is the source address of the received packets, which tells this sending entity's flow apart from any other sender on the group. A receiver behind an AMT relay compares against the encapsulated IP header, which keeps the original source address ( Section 5.1.6). Because the sending entity knows its own source address for every endpoint, the PA message is identical on every endpoint, and its one version sequence applies everywhere, so a newer version overrides an older one on all endpoints alike ( Clauses 10.2.3 and 10.3.9.3). Repair flows are not Assets, and the MP table does not list them; their in-band signaling is the AL-FEC message of Section 8.3, which travels on the same sub-flow.

The publisher MUST send a PA message on the sub-flow ahead of the MPU metadata (FT=0) data unit of every MPU of every track that it sends to an endpoint, later than the FT=0 data unit of the previous MPU of the same track, and ahead of any other signaling message sent for that MPU, such as the AL-FEC message, so that a receiver joining any endpoint at an MPU boundary holds the mapping before that MPU's media and other signaling; Clause 10.3.2.1 requires a receiver to process a PA message before any other signaling message. A receiver joined to several endpoints receives each packet of the sub-flow once per endpoint, as identical copies with the same packet_sequence_number; it acts on one copy of each packet, whether a PA message or an AL-FEC message, and ignores the rest. An endpoint that lists only fec-repair tracks (a repair-only endpoint, Section 4) carries no Asset and need not carry the sub-flow. A receiver that holds the catalog routes a repair-only endpoint's packetId values from the catalog ( Section 4). A receiver without the catalog cannot discover a repair-only endpoint, because the MP table locates only Assets and the AL-FEC message names a repair flow by packetId without a location, so repair carried on a repair-only endpoint reaches only catalog-holding receivers.

For a receiver that holds the catalog, the endpoint's packetId values remain authoritative: it routes packets by them as above, needs no PA message, and handles packet_id 0 per Section 3.1. A PA message is never carried as a MoQ object ( Section 4.2).

The Multicast QUIC row corresponds to , which adds QUIC's per-packet AEAD and integrity. The mapping of MMTP packets onto its DATAGRAM frames, and the use of FEC on that channel, are described, informatively, in Section 3.4.

section.name: Explicit Congestion Notification
section.t: A sender SHOULD set ECT(0) in the ECN field of every data datagram of a protected flow () and of every manifest record of the flow, twins included, so that a queue that implements Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) marks such a datagram Congestion Experienced (CE) where it would otherwise have dropped it ( Section 5); such a queue drops a Not-ECT datagram as it would without ECN. A receiver that can read the ECN field MUST treat a datagram that arrives marked CE as it treats a lost one in endpoint selection and in the failover from multicast to MoQ unicast (), and in no other reaction to loss. On a protected flow it so treats only a data datagram it admits and a record it verifies (steps 1 and 2 of ); a mark on any other datagram on port counts toward nothing, since an injector that spoofs S can set it, so a marked datagram that expires from a hold queue is one loss, by its expiry (), and a marked record dropped before its signature verifies, or as a copy, is the loss an unmarked one would be: one, by its drop, where the port bucket dropped it for want of a token and the receiver counts such drops (), and none otherwise. A multicast sender gets no feedback, so the receivers' reaction stands in for the sender's: it is the receiver-driven congestion control of Section 4.1, responding to a mark as to a drop, as Section 5 asks of the end systems of an ECN-capable transport, and it departs from Section 3.1.7, which requires CE feedback to the sender. A receiver that cannot read the ECN field, as one that receives native SSM through the UDPMessage of , which carries no ECN field, takes a CE-marked datagram for an unmarked one, and so reacts to a marking queue's congestion only once that queue drops. A receiver that reads a mark still processes the datagram, and it MUST NOT count the mark toward adding repair, whether a repair layer, a repair-only endpoint ( Section 4) or a unicast repair FETCH (), or against dropping repair, since repair added or held on a path that is losing packets to congestion adds to the congestion ( Section 7.4). A receiver MUST NOT wait for the sender to lower its rate in response to the marks: no mark reaches the sender, and a mark set upstream of a replication point reaches every receiver below it, each of which reacts to it as above. An AMT gateway () MUST carry the ECN field of the encapsulated datagram through decapsulation per , as Section 6.1.4 applies it to AMT, and declares that support with the E flag of Section 6.1.4.2. Section 6.1.4 recommends the same support in an AMT relay without requiring it: a relay that has it copies the ECN field into the outer header for a gateway that sets the E flag, and one that lacks it clears the outer ECN field ( Section 6.1.4.1), so congestion between that relay and the gateway reaches the receiver as loss, while a mark set before the relay still arrives in the encapsulated header. The digest of covers the addresses, the ports and the payload of a datagram, not its ECN field, so a mark set on the path never fails a digest.

section.name: Multi-Path Delivery
section.t: The same media content (source and repair) can be transmitted over both MoQ unicast (QUIC/WebTransport) and multicast (UDP/SSM/AMT) paths simultaneously. Because the same MMTP packets are used on all transports, receivers can combine symbols from any path for FEC recovery ( Section 5.5).
When symbols arrive from multiple paths simultaneously, receivers:

ol.li: MUST deduplicate symbols within one FEC instance ( Section 5.1) -- a source track's base instance together with all of its repair layers, or its keyframe overlay ( Section 7.4) -- using SS_ID as the unique key of a source symbol and (SS_Start, RS_ID) as that of a repair symbol ( Section 5.5)

MAY combine source and repair symbols received on different paths in either direction: source symbols via multicast with repair symbols via MoQ/QUIC, or source symbols via reliable MoQ/QUIC with repair symbols via lossy multicast -- skipping FEC decoding when all source symbols arrive reliably

section.t: Multicast-to-unicast failover: if multicast reception fails, a subscriber falls back to MoQ/QUIC unicast. It resumes a unicast subscription that it paused when it switched to multicast, as Section 6.3 describes. Otherwise it subscribes again, with a SUBSCRIBE whose LOCATION_FILTER parameter ( Section 9.20.9) sets where delivery starts, using one of the joins of Section 3.5:

ul.li: Next Object (Location Filter Type 0x05) starts at the live edge. Delivery can begin in the middle of a group.

Next Object together with a FILL_PARAMETERS parameter ( Section 9.20.15) whose LOCATION_FILTER is Relative Start (0x01) with StartGroup 1 also delivers the current group from its start, on a fill fetch stream ( Section 3.4). This is the join of Section 6.1, and the one to use when the receiver cannot decode from the middle of a group.
Relative Start (0x01) with StartGroup 0 starts at the next group.

section.t: No coordinate mapping between multicast SS_IDs and MoQ Group IDs is needed, because the publisher resolves each of these filters against its Largest Object ( Section 3.1.4). Failover replaces the multicast path; it is distinct from per-block unicast repair (Section 6.2), which leaves the multicast subscription in place.

section.name: Packaging Negotiation
section.t: Packaging is advertised per track in the catalog, and a subscriber subscribes by name to the tracks whose packaging it supports. The altGroup catalog field ( Section 5.2.12, profiled in Section 4.4) groups alternatives of the same content in different packaging formats.

section.name: Per-Block Unicast Repair
section.t: A multicast or AMT receiver repairs every FEC block in-band from the repair symbols it receives on its multicast paths. For a block that in-band FEC leaves unrecovered at its FEC deadline, a receiver that holds a MoQ session (Section 1.1) applies the receiver repair policy of Section 6 of , which repairs a keyframe-bearing block by a FETCH of the block's repair-track group. That group's ID is the block's extended SS_Start ( Section 7.6): the SS_Start from the Repair FEC Payload ID of a multicast repair packet of the block, extended with the wrap epoch to a value in [0, 2^62). MoQ Transport Group IDs range up to 2^64 - 1 ( Section 8.1); repair Group IDs use only [0, 2^62), as Section 7.6 specifies. A receiver that takes its repair from multicast has usually received no repair-track Group ID over MoQ. Before its first FETCH it therefore establishes the wrap epoch, as Section 7.6 specifies, unless it has received such a Group ID or has observed the FEC instance from its first block. To do so, it sends a TRACK_STATUS request for the repair track ( Section 9.13). The epoch comes from the Group of the Largest Object ( Section 3.1.4) carried in the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter ( Section 9.20.17) of the REQUEST_OK (TRACK_STATUS_OK) that answers it. For lost source packets whose block it has not delimited, because it holds no repair packet of that block, the receiver instead fetches the Group range that Section 7.7 derives from a lost SS_ID. No other coordinate mapping is needed, and the returned symbols are deduplicated per item 1 of Section 6. A receiver without a MoQ session cannot request unicast repair; it relies on in-band FEC and, where published, the keyframe overlay ( Section 7.4).

A relay that does not hold the requested objects fetches them upstream ( Sections 3.2.3 and 7.6). A FETCH for a repair-track group that neither the relay nor any publisher upstream of it still holds fails or returns none of the group's objects, and the receiver then treats the block as unrecoverable. How long relays and the original publisher keep repair-track groups is their own policy.

section.name: Unicast Subscriptions After a Switch to Multicast
section.t: After a receiver switches to multicast (Section 4.1), it still holds the unicast subscriptions that delivered the same media before the switch: to the tracks it now receives on multicast or to their loc or cmaf alternatives (Section 4.1), to the repair tracks of such a loc or cmaf alternative, and to the repair tracks that its multicast endpoints now carry. While these subscriptions forward objects, the receiver gets the media twice, and the network still carries the unicast copy that the multicast path replaces. Once multicast delivery of a track is verified, for example by the receipt on multicast of a complete group or a complete FEC block of the track, the receiver SHOULD pause these subscriptions or end them:

ul.li: To pause a subscription, the receiver sends a REQUEST_UPDATE with the FORWARD parameter set to 0 ( Sections 3.1.1 and 9.20.18). The subscription stays Established, and the publisher sends no objects on it. Failover then needs no new SUBSCRIBE.
To end a subscription, the receiver sends STOP_SENDING ( Section 3.1).

section.t: The receiver does not pause its other subscriptions, such as those to the catalog track, any manifest track (Section 7.2.5), and any repair layer that no endpoint it holds carries and that it combines with multicast source symbols (Section 6, item 2; Section 4).

On failover (Section 6), the receiver resumes a paused subscription with a REQUEST_UPDATE that sets FORWARD to 1. FILL_PARAMETERS carried while a subscription is paused opens no fill fetch stream, and resuming without re-sending FILL_PARAMETERS opens none either ( Section 3.4.1). A receiver that needs the current group from its start therefore sends FILL_PARAMETERS, as in the join of Section 6, in a further REQUEST_UPDATE after it receives the REQUEST_UPDATE_OK for the update that resumed the subscription. A receiver that ended its subscriptions subscribes again as Section 6 describes.
Pausing or ending these subscriptions does not affect per-block unicast repair (Section 6.2), which uses FETCH.

section.name: Multicast Security
section.t: SSM inherently limits traffic to authorized sources via (S,G) filtering. Receivers MAY detect replayed packets by tracking the MMTP Packet Sequence Number per packet_id within one (source address, groupAddress, port) tuple and discarding duplicates and packets outside a bounded reordering window. The source address is that of the received packets, the same address Section 5 matches: it equals sourceAddress on an SSM endpoint and is read from each packet on an ASM endpoint, so two sending entities that share an ASM group and each use the same packet_id are tracked separately. For AMT, the gateway reads the source address from the encapsulated header and trusts the relay to have joined that source per ; the relay authenticates nothing it forwards, so an AMT receiver of a protected flow checks the source itself ().

section.name: Content Authentication
section.t: Multicast UDP delivery lacks the integrity protection that QUIC provides on unicast paths. This section defines "bc-provenance" version 2, a manifest-provenance authentication profile. For each protected flow the publisher computes a digest over every data datagram the flow emits, repair symbols included; collects digests into windows of at most 37 datagrams or manifestTimerMs, whichever closes first; places each window in a fixed-layout manifest record; signs the record with a dedicated broadcast Ed25519 key under a network-identity prefix; and emits the record in band, on the flow's own (S, G, port), immediately before the datagrams it covers, followed by a second copy. Receivers verify one signature per window, hash each datagram once, and admit a datagram to reassembly, FEC decode or delivery only after its digest matches an entry of a verified manifest.

The digest pseudoheader, the hold queue and the consume-on-admission rule are those of AMBI ( Sections 3.4.2 and 3.2); the signed record is a multicast-carried manifest delivery of the kind that AMBI Section 2.1.1 leaves to another specification, and this document carries it in band, on the flow's own (S, G, port).
The digest algorithm is carried in the signed record as a Named Information Suite ID (); SHA-256 is mandatory to implement.
The record, digest pseudoheader, signature prefix and hash registry do not depend on MoQ: they are the format of , restated here by value, and , and bind them to MoQ.

All multi-octet integers are unsigned and big-endian; u8, u16, u32 and u64 are unsigned integers of that width; lp16(x) is a u16 octet count followed by the octets of x; a string is its UTF-8 octets; H is the function selected by the record's hash_alg (), with a 32-octet output. Test vectors are in .

section.name: Protected Flows and Sequence Numbers
section.t: The protected unit is a flow: every datagram the sending entity emits to one endpoint (S, G, port) of whose auth member is present (), other than the manifest records () it emits there; such a datagram is a data datagram. That is the datagrams of every track the endpoint lists, repair tracks included, and the MMTP signaling sub-flow on packet_id 0 () where the endpoint carries it. A track carried on several endpoints is in a separate flow on each. A packet of a listed track that another path delivers to a consumer protected under the flow, one that has admitted a datagram of it, is a datagram of the flow as well (step 2 of ). A flow has one port, which no other flow of the same (S, G) shares (), so no port of an (S, G) carries the data or the records of two flows; its sequence counter (below) and its mseq counter () are kept per (kid, epoch). mseq starts at any value and increases by one for every window the flow closes under one (kid, epoch), in emission order, as the replay floor of step 1 of and the twin deadline of assume.

sequence is a 64-bit counter the sender assigns per (flow, kid, epoch): it starts at any value and increases by one for every data datagram the flow emits, in emission order, repair symbols and signaling datagrams included. It is carried only in manifest records, never in data datagrams, and is unrelated to MoQ group_id and object_id. Digest i of a record covers sequence = first_seq + i, so one window is a contiguous run of the flow. A window MAY span a MoQ group boundary. A datagram the sender emits twice (a carousel) has two sequences and two digests. Neither counter wraps within an epoch: a sender ends the epoch (the record whose flags bit 0 is set, ) before either would exceed 2^64 - 1, and the comparisons this profile states on them are integer comparisons evaluated without unsigned underflow or overflow.

section.name: Digest
section.t: Every data datagram the sender emits in a protected flow, repair symbols included, has a digest; a manifest record is not a data datagram and has none:

payload is the entire UDP payload as transmitted, including the trailing Source FEC Payload ID when the packet's FEC Type is 1 ( Section 7.2), so a verified digest also authenticates the FEC block assignment of a received packet. A packet the decoder recovers carries no Source FEC Payload ID and none is re-appended for delivery ( Section 7.1); when its admission needs a digest, the receiver appends the base SS_ID its position in the base block implies, for the hash only ().
pseudoheader is the AMBI pseudoheader of Section 3.4.2, restated here by value since that draft has expired:
section.artwork: pseudoheader = S # 4 octets (IPv4) or 16 octets (IPv6) || G # 4 or 16 octets, same family as S || 0x00 # zeroes || 0x11 # protocol, UDP || u16(payload_length) # length of payload in octets || u16(src_port) || u16(dst_port) || u32(streamId)
section.t: Addresses are in native width, never IPv4-mapped. S is the address from which the sending entity transmits the flow (): the endpoint's sourceAddress on an SSM endpoint and its auth.senderAddress on an ASM endpoint (). src_port and dst_port are both the endpoint's port: the sender MUST emit every datagram of the flow from UDP source port port. streamId is the endpoint's auth.streamId. Every input is catalog-declared, and a receiver without the catalog holds the same values from its out-of-band provisioning (), so for a datagram of the flow delivered over a unicast MoQ path or an MMTP broadcast the receiver forms the same pseudoheader and one digest verifies the same bytes on every path (; step 2 of ).

section.name: Manifest Record
section.t: A manifest record is one UDP datagram that the sender emits from UDP source port port on the protected flow's own (S, G, port), interleaved with the flow's data datagrams. Every field except the signature is at a fixed offset, and the signature is the last 64 octets.

tr.td: epoch, increments on sender restart and key change
mseq, manifest counter, monotonic per (flow, kid, epoch)
sent, emission time in POSIX seconds (below)

section.t: Length is 132 + 32 x count octets. The cap of 37 digests is an MTU choice: the 1316-octet maximum is 1344 octets on the wire with IPv4 and UDP headers and 1364 with IPv6, which leaves room for AMT encapsulation on a 1500-octet path.

magic is how a receiver tells a record from a data datagram on port (), so a sender MUST NOT emit a data datagram whose first four octets are "MHM2". No data datagram of a flow begins with them: each is an MMTP version 0 packet (; Section 3.1), whose leading version field excludes the octet 0x4D ("M"). An application that listens on port and does not implement this profile receives the records and their twins as well; each reads as an MMTP packet of version 1, which a receiver of rejects before parsing its type field (its Section 3.1).

flags: bit 0, the least significant bit of the octet (mask 0x01), epoch end (); bits 1 to 7 reserved, MUST be zero on send and ignored on receipt. A sender SHOULD set bit 0 in the record of the last window of every epoch whose end it plans (a key change, a counter that would exceed 2^64 - 1 (), an orderly restart); an epoch that ends unplanned, as at a crash, has no such record.

sent is the sender's clock when the record is signed, truncated to whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z with leap seconds excluded, from a clock synchronized to UTC within 1 s; the twin of a record () carries the original's value. It is a count of seconds, not the 16.16 NTP short format, so it wraps in 2106 rather than every 18.2 hours. A sender whose clock is further off than the tolerance of makes its flow unverifiable to receivers that check freshness.

All records of one flow carry the same hash_alg for the life of a stream generation (streamId, ); a change of algorithm is a new generation. epoch never decreases under one kid: a sending entity MUST NOT reuse an epoch under a kid, across generations or restarts, and a generation that would start below the kid's last epoch starts under a new kid ().

section.name: Signature Context Binding
section.t: The signature is computed over:
section.artwork: signed_message = "mcast-manifest-v2" || 0x00 # 18-octet label || u32(streamId) || S # 4 or 16 octets || G # 4 or 16 octets || u16(port) || record[0 .. len - 64)
section.t: with S, G, streamId and port as declared for the endpoint (, ). The prefix binds the flow's network identity; a receiver needs no catalog state to check it beyond those four values, which a MoQ receiver takes from the catalog and a broadcast-only receiver from its provisioning (). The MoQ context is bound inside the record by ctx:
section.artwork:
ctx = H("BCPV2-ctx" || u16(f) || f * lp16(field) # namespace, in order || u16(n) || n * u16(packetId) # ascending || params_hash)
params_hash = H("BCPV2-params" || lp16(codec) || u32(timescale) || u32(groupDurationTicks) || m * ( lp16(scheme) || u32(sourceSymbols) || u32(repairSymbols) || u32(symbolSize) || u32(interleaveDepthMs) ))
section.t: both with the record's hash_alg. The field values are the f Track Namespace Fields, in order, of the one MoQ namespace the sending entity serves (): the Track Namespace of the catalog track (), which every track listed on an endpoint shares (; Section 5.2.2); each field is the octets MOQT carries for it. The packetId values are those of the endpoint's tracks (), n of them in ascending order. params_hash is taken from the catalog entry of the endpoint's lowest-packetId media track or, for an endpoint that lists only fec-repair tracks, from the catalog entry of the source track that its lowest-packetId repair track repairs: the track its source names or, where it carries none, the track one of whose FEC instances names it as its repairTrack ( Section 3.2). codec is that entry's MSF field; timescale is its timescale and groupDurationTicks its group duration in timescale ticks, both as Section 4.4.2 resolves them; the m tuples are the entry's FEC instances, the members of its fec array ( Section 3.1), in ascending instanceId, one tuple per instance, each tuple's five values being the instance's same-named fields, scheme the registered scheme identifier ( Section 15.2); neither m nor an instanceId is encoded, and the concatenation is unambiguous because every field but the length-prefixed scheme is fixed-width. blockProfile, reorderToleranceMs, instanceId, repairTrack, symbolTrack and the per-track fields of , an enhancement layer's repairSymbols included, are deliberately unbound, although blockProfile and reorderToleranceMs are part of the instance's geometry ( Section 10.1): params_hash binds the five per-instance values that -01 bound, so the -01 values of params_hash and ctx are unchanged (). An absent interleaveDepthMs is encoded as u32(0); an entry with no fec array, or an empty one, is encoded as lp16("none") followed by four u32(0), distinct from every instance because Section 15.2 reserves "none" and no scheme may take it; an entry for which Section 4.4.2 resolves no timescale or no group duration, as it need not for a track that is not mmtp-packaged (), is encoded as u32(0) for that value. A flow carried without a MoQ catalog sets ctx to 32 zero octets. A MoQ receiver recomputes ctx from the catalog and MUST reject a record whose ctx differs (); a receiver without the catalog carries ctx blind. A valid (record, datagrams) pair therefore cannot be replayed onto another endpoint, stream generation, broadcast, key or epoch; sent () bounds replay within an epoch to the clock tolerance of .

section.name: Emission and Cadence
section.t: A sender closes a window after 37 datagrams or after manifestTimerMs since the window opened, whichever comes first; the timer governs only while the flow emits at most 37 datagrams per manifestTimerMs (1850 per second at the default, about 21 Mbit/s of 1400-octet datagrams), and the count cap governs above that. A sender MUST NOT close more than 64 + V x t windows on one flow in any interval of t seconds, a long-run rate of at most V per second, V being the rate at which the verification budgets of step 1 of refill, computed from the endpoint's bandwidth; a sender above that ceiling starves its own receivers, whose budgets drop its records and expire its windows as loss (). A sender MAY raise manifestTimerMs to at most maxAuthDelayMs / 4 on low-rate flows.

The signed record MUST be transmitted immediately before the first datagram it covers (only the twin of an earlier window MAY come between them), so the sender holds at most one window of data. A twin, a byte-identical copy of the record, MUST be transmitted after the last datagram the record covers, no later than maxAuthDelayMs / 2 after the record and before the signed record of window mseq + 64, so that at most 63 later records precede it and it arrives above the replay floor of , which only the records arriving on port raise, however fast the flow closes windows; RECOMMENDED is to transmit it immediately after the signed record of window mseq + 2 and before the first datagram that record covers, or on its own at the maxAuthDelayMs / 2 deadline when window mseq + 2 has not closed by then. The two copies then bracket the window's datagrams: a contiguous loss burst that removes both copies has removed every datagram between them, and a datagram that survives such a burst has a usable copy on one side of it, whatever the flow's rate and timer; only two separate losses can leave an arriving datagram without a copy, and then at most 37 datagrams expire from the hold queues (). Every twin of an epoch MUST be transmitted before the first record of a later epoch, since a receiver drops the records of an earlier epoch once its grace period ends (); every twin of the epoch not yet transmitted when its last datagram has been sent, the twin of the record whose flags bit 0 is set included, follows that datagram at once. A receiver handles either copy by step 1 of and drops the second with one lookup and one hash.

At 37 digests per window, a record and its twin cost about 71 octets per 1400-octet datagram (5.1%); data datagrams are untouched. Manifest records MUST NOT be FEC-protected; the twin is their loss remedy.

A publisher MAY mirror the same record octets as objects on a MoQ manifest track (one record per object; a record goes in manifest-track group N, N being the Group ID of the latest packet, emitted at or before the window's first datagram, of the track whose catalog entry supplies params_hash (), or of that track's first group of the stream generation where none precedes) for unicast subscribers. A packet of a track the endpoint lists that reaches a consumer protected under the flow is a datagram of the flow on a MoQ unicast path too (step 2 of ), and the mirror is its only source of records while the multicast path delivers none, during the join of and after the failover of . Without a manifestTrack a track's unicast fallback is a MoQ subscription outside this profile, protected by the MoQ session alone, so a publisher that wants the fallback verified against its records MUST name one. Records read from the manifest track charge a verification budget of their own, not the flow's port budget (); a receiver that reads the manifest track while joined to the multicast path sees each record first on the shorter path and drops the later copy as already verified, matching its digests only where it raises the mirror's lead (step 1 of ), so where the mirror leads port it widens, by the mirror's lead and under the bound below, the pending expiry of a mirrored record's entries and the time for which it keeps a digest it admits recorded as admitted: a relay copy admitted first would otherwise leave the multicast copy, arriving up to the lead later, to be held and to expire as loss (steps 1 and 2 of ). The lead of a record is unknown when its entries are inserted, so the receiver keeps the lead as a per-flow value: the largest interval it has measured in the stream generation from the arrival of a record on the mirror to the arrival of the first copy on port, which the lookup drops (a later copy on that path, the twin or one replayed within the retention, measures nothing; step 1 keeps the time and path of arrival, and a digest of the record's bytes, with each verified (kid, epoch, mseq) for this), each interval rounded up to a multiple of manifestTimerMs before it is compared with the lead (so the lead rises at most 5000 / manifestTimerMs times in a stream generation, 250 at the default, however a relay paces the mirror; step 1), and the bound below until it has measured one; a copy that raises the lead, byte-identical to the verified record, re-admits or re-inserts, under the raised lead and ahead of the datagrams they cover, the digests of that record and of every record verified on the manifest track within the raised lead before now whose first copy has not yet arrived, for the pairs that have admitted nothing and are not pending, widens the pending entries of those records by the raised lead, and records again as admitted, under the raised lead, the digests of the pairs that have, so that a mirror whose lead grows past the one measured, within the bound below, costs the datagrams of those records nothing, a late copy of a datagram a pair has admitted is dropped rather than held, and a copy replayed within the retention re-admits nothing (step 1). A receiver that reads no manifest track applies no lead, nor does one that will not join the multicast path; one that may yet join applies the bound until it has measured a lead, since the multicast copies of the datagrams its relay delivers before the join arrive after it. The timers of are wall-clock bounds; a relay-buffered QUIC path can deliver records later than maxAuthDelayMs, or the datagrams of a window later than the record that covers them, the manifest track and the media tracks being separate streams, and a unicast receiver SHOULD widen its hold, and the freshness tolerance of step 1 of for the records it reads from the manifest track, accordingly, by a widening W of at most 5 s (the bound), a receiver that applies no lead widening the pending expiry of a mirrored record's entries by W as well (step 1), since no lead covers the datagrams its relay delivers after the records that cover them: the widening is also its exposure at join to windows that much older served by its relay (), a record on port keeps the unwidened tolerance and pending expiry as the multicast path's hold queue keeps the unwidened expiry, and a receiver that needs more is replaying (). The bound caps the lead as well: a relay that leads the multicast path by more than the bound plus maxAuthDelayMs outruns the admitted digests the lead widens, and by more than that plus 2 x manifestTimerMs the pending entries as well, and the copy on port of a record it mirrors that far ahead, which the receiver keeps verified for as long as the freshness check of step 1 would pass it, or for as long after that as its mseq stays above the manifest track's replay floor (), is dropped by the lookup of step 1 while so kept and by that check after, and, the lead standing at the bound, admits nothing either way, so the multicast copies of the datagrams of those records are held and expire from the multicast path's hold queue, loss for the failover (); the lead being the multicast path's lag behind the mirror, such a path fails over on its own latency on a receiver that checks freshness. One that skips the check (the Clock paragraph of ) keeps the record verified 7 s + maxAuthDelayMs after its arrival on the manifest track, or for as long after that as its mseq stays above the manifest track's replay floor (the state list of that section), so under a relay leading by more than the longer of the two the copy on port misses the lookup, meets no freshness check and is verified anew there, from that path's budget, admitting the datagrams of its window as any record on port does: such a receiver fails over on a lead between the bound plus maxAuthDelayMs and that retention and, under a larger one, verifies every record on both paths instead; on a flow whose 64 windows outlast 7 s + maxAuthDelayMs, the floor keeps the record verified until its copy arrives under any lead shorter than 64 windows, the lookup drops the copy, and such a receiver fails over as one that checks freshness does. Under a lead beyond that retention such a receiver still loses windows at each epoch change, and so may fail over there: those of the previous epoch's records whose copies reach port past that epoch's deadline (step 1 of ), and those of most of its 64 latest records, whose copies the lookup drops because that epoch's replay floor, raised by no later record, keeps them verified.

section.name: Catalog Signaling
section.t: The auth member of the multicast object () declares the profile and its keys; the auth member of an endpoint object marks that endpoint's flow as protected and carries the flow's parameters:
Members of multicast.auth:
scheme, version (REQUIRED): "bc-provenance", 2.

sig (string, REQUIRED): "ed25519" . A receiver that finds scheme, version or sig absent, or with a value it does not implement, admits nothing from the broadcast, pinned or not, and treats every endpoint of the multicast object as one that yields no data ().

keys (array, REQUIRED): one to four {kid, publicKey, firstEpoch} objects. kid is an unsigned 32-bit integer carried in the clear in every record; publicKey is the 32-octet Ed25519 public key, base64url-encoded without padding ( Section 5); firstEpoch is the first epoch the key signs. A key signs the epochs from its firstEpoch up to, but not including, the next larger firstEpoch in the array, and the key with the largest firstEpoch signs every later epoch. kid values MUST be unique within a broadcast and firstEpoch values MUST be distinct within the array. A receiver that takes its keys from a catalog whose keys is absent, has no or more than four entries, repeats a kid or a firstEpoch, or names a kid or firstEpoch that is not an unsigned 32-bit integer or a publicKey that does not decode to 32 octets holds no key set for the broadcast: it admits nothing and treats every endpoint of the multicast object as one that yields no data (), as it does on a flow whose records carry an algorithm it does not implement (); a receiver that pins keys is unaffected, since its key set comes from the pin. A receiver drops, before verification, a record whose epoch is outside its kid's range (), so a retired key cannot carry a receiver past its successor's firstEpoch.

minEpoch (integer, REQUIRED): the lowest epoch a receiver accepts at join (step 1 of ); after its first verified record the current epoch is the floor, with the previous epoch admitted on port until that path's grace period ends, or while that path has started none, and never past the bound of plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the current epoch became current, and on the manifest track within the earlier-started of the two paths' periods (step 1). The publisher MUST write the current epoch at every epoch change, sender restart included, so a joiner with a current catalog cannot be fed an earlier epoch. The publisher MUST keep every endpoint of the multicast object at one epoch and change it on all of them together: this minEpoch, and the per-kid epoch floor that a receiver which pins keys keeps for the broadcast (), bound each of them at join, so the records of an endpoint left at a lower epoch than another are dropped at join. A receiver whose catalog declares no minEpoch, or one that is not an unsigned 32-bit integer, admits nothing from the broadcast, pinned or not, and treats every endpoint of the multicast object as one that yields no data ().

Members of an endpoint's auth; a protected endpoint MUST also declare bandwidth, the sender's ceiling for the flow rather than its average, since it bounds the receiver's hold queues and sets its verification budgets ():

ul.li: streamId (integer, REQUIRED): 32-bit value chosen per stream generation, bound into every digest and signature.

senderAddress (string, REQUIRED on an ASM endpoint, MUST NOT appear on an SSM endpoint): the address from which the sending entity transmits this endpoint's flow, S of ; on an SSM endpoint S is sourceAddress.
maxAuthDelayMs (integer, OPTIONAL, default 200, range 50 to 1000): how long a receiver holds a datagram whose digest has not arrived.
manifestTimerMs (integer, OPTIONAL, default 20, at least 1): the window timer of .
manifestTrack (string, OPTIONAL): the MoQ track mirroring the records ().

section.t: A receiver keeps the values of the catalog it holds until a later catalog or a re-provisioning replaces them, and a record whose kid it holds triggers no re-fetch (). For one catalog lifetime after it publishes a new bandwidth, maxAuthDelayMs or manifestTimerMs for an endpoint, a publisher therefore keeps within the old value as well as the new one: it sends above the old bandwidth only once that lifetime has passed. A receiver that holds an endpoint's old streamId verifies no record of the new generation, a move to another hash suite included (), until a catalog carrying the new value reaches it. A change of a value that ctx binds (), such as a track added to the endpoint's tracks, allows no such overlap, since a record carries one ctx: a receiver whose catalog predates the change drops every record signed after it, and one whose catalog carries the change every record signed before it, at the ctx check of step 1 of , so the change interrupts the flow at each receiver until its catalog and the records agree.

A protected endpoint's port MUST differ from the port of every other endpoint of the same (S, G) in the catalog, so that no port of an (S, G) carries the data or the records of two flows (). A receiver MUST ignore () every protected endpoint that shares its (S, G, port) with another endpoint, and every protected endpoint whose bandwidth is absent or is not a positive integer, whose port is not an integer from 1 to 65535, whose streamId is absent or is not an unsigned 32-bit integer, whose senderAddress is absent on an ASM endpoint or present on an SSM endpoint, or whose manifestTimerMs is below 1, and it clamps a maxAuthDelayMs outside 50 to 1000 to the nearer bound, as the browser profile of does; it never uses an out-of-range value. Two ASM endpoints whose senderAddress differ MAY share groupAddress and port; the source check of separates them.

When the multicast object carries auth, every endpoint of the multicast object MUST carry auth; a receiver MUST ignore () an endpoint that lacks it, so every multicast datagram it consumes from the sending entity is in a protected flow and reaches a decoder only through . An endpoint that carries auth when the multicast object does not is ignored likewise, since it names no key.

section.name: Receiver Enforcement and State
section.t: A receiver that implements this profile enforces it: a datagram of a protected flow is admitted only after its digest matches an entry of a verified record, and there is no verify-and-report mode. A receiver MUST be able to pin "authentication required" for a broadcast independently of the catalog. A receiver without the catalog (a broadcast-only receiver, or native SSM reception without a MoQ session) MUST be provisioned out of band with the keys, firstEpoch included, and minEpoch and, per protected flow, the streamId, S, G, port and bandwidth the catalog would declare (), and any non-default maxAuthDelayMs and manifestTimerMs: the record carries none of them, and a broadcast carries the flow on those addresses and ports or not at all (); keys are never taken from a carrier's signaling. A receiver that pins keys takes the key set, firstEpoch included, from the pin rather than from the catalog, and MUST keep with the pin, across sessions, the highest epoch it has verified under each pinned kid; in step 1 below it drops, at join, a record whose epoch is below that value for its kid, so a catalog that carries a lower minEpoch cannot reopen an epoch a verified record has closed. The pin stores no value read from a catalog: every receiver takes minEpoch from the catalog it fetched, or provisions it with the keys, and it bounds that session only. A receiver with no pin is protected at its first join against an earlier epoch only as far as that catalog is. A receiver that implements no algorithm a flow's records carry verifies nothing on that flow: it admits nothing and treats the endpoint as one that yields no data ().

On an ASM endpoint a receiver MUST discard, before any parsing or hashing, a datagram on port whose IP source address is not senderAddress; behind an AMT relay the address is that of the encapsulated header (). On an SSM endpoint reached natively the network enforces the source and a receiver SHOULD still discard a datagram whose source address is not sourceAddress; a receiver reached through an AMT gateway MUST discard it, since nothing upstream of its gateway filters the encapsulated source address and does not authenticate Multicast Data messages. A receiver MUST likewise discard, before any parsing or hashing, a datagram on port whose IP destination address, behind an AMT relay that of the encapsulated header, is not G, since flows of one S in different groups may share a port; a datagram that passes both checks belongs to the flow (S, G, port) with S as in .

State per flow: the current epoch with the kid that set it, the time at which that epoch became current, per path (port and the manifest track) the grace period that ends maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the first record of the current epoch verified on that path or dropped there by the already-verified lookup of step 1 as its byte-identical copy, and, until the period on port ends or the previous epoch's deadline passes, the previous epoch, the deadline being the bound of plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the current epoch became current (step 1; a record on port meets its own path's period and the deadline, one read from the manifest track the earlier-started of the two periods, which ends before the deadline); the flow's hash_alg, fixed by its first verified record; per (kid, epoch) the verified mseq values above the replay floor of the path they arrived on, and those verified on the manifest track for as long as the freshness check of step 1 would pass a copy of them on port, their sent within 7 s + maxAuthDelayMs behind the receiver's clock, or that long after their arrival on the manifest track where the receiver skips that check, whatever the floor (so that the lookup of step 1 still meets, and measures the lead from, a copy on port arriving after 64 or more further records were verified on the mirror, and drops as already verified every copy that check would pass: one arriving more than the bound of plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the mirror's copy, the lead standing at the bound, then admits nothing, and the datagrams it covers expire, as that section says, rather than being verified anew on port; where the lead stands below the bound, the first such copy raises it to the bound and handles the record's pairs again as step 1 says; a receiver that skips the check verifies anew a copy arriving after the retention and below the manifest track's replay floor, save a copy of the previous epoch arriving past that epoch's deadline, which step 1 drops, dropping by the lookup one that arrives above the floor, as that section also says), each with the time and path of its arrival, its sent, which that retention reads, the hash_alg digest of the record's bytes, per pair of the record, whether a datagram has been admitted against it and, for a record verified on the manifest track whose first copy on port has not yet arrived, the record's pairs, which a raise of the lead re-handles (steps 1 and 2), per path the highest_mseq that the records arriving on it have raised (step 1) and, once a verified record has flags bit 0 set, the mseq that closed it; the verification budgets of step 1, one for port and one for the manifest track, each with a count of the records it dropped; the mirror's lead (), a multiple of manifestTimerMs or the bound, and whether the stream generation has measured one, the bound of that section applying until it has and zero on a receiver that reads no manifest track or will not join the multicast path; a pending table of (digest, sequence, expiry) entries, each naming the record and the pair that inserted it, an entry whose expiry the mirror's lead or W widened keeping its insertion time as well (step 1); the digests recorded as admitted, each until the expiry set when it was recorded, the time of recording plus maxAuthDelayMs plus the mirror's lead then in force, a copy on port that raises the lead recording again the digests of the marked pairs it handles (steps 1 and 2); for each open block of a protected consumer, the number of decodes, at most two, taken with the help of symbols of unlisted tracks (step 2) that have left it unrecovered, block state under the bound of Section 9.4 released with the block (step 2); on a receiver that can request unicast repair, for each open block that has an FEC deadline, the admission time of the first packet, source or repair, admitted into it, or of the packet that stands for it under step 2 (the source packet of highest SS_ID admitted at or below its lower bounding packet, or the packet admitted above it where the instance has admitted none below), and for each base instance the admission time of the source packet of highest SS_ID it has admitted in the stream generation, kept under the serial number arithmetic of Section 7.6 (step 2); two hold queues of (digest, datagram, expiry) entries in arrival order, each also keeping whether its datagram arrived marked CE (), digest being absent from an entry until the first record of the flow is verified (step 2): one for the datagrams a MoQ unicast path delivers and the packets the base instance recovers with the help of a symbol that path delivered (step 2), and one for the rest. State per receiver, shared by its flows: the time of the last catalog re-fetch that an unknown kid triggered (key rotation, below), and the per-kid epoch floor kept with a key pin, one for each broadcast whose keys the receiver pins and shared only by that broadcast's flows, even where two broadcasts list the same keys. The per-flow state belongs to the stream generation (): when the streamId the catalog, or a receiver's provisioning, declares for the endpoint changes, the receiver discards every per-flow item above but the two verification budgets and their counts and the hold queues (the current and previous epoch, hash_alg, the per-(kid, epoch) mseq state, the mirror's lead, the pending table with the entries kept for unicast repair, the admitted digests, the per-block decode counts and the per-block and per-instance admission times), clears the digest of every held datagram, and processes the next record as the first of the flow under the join-time floors of step 1.

A datagram on port whose first four octets are the ASCII octets "MHM2" is a record candidate and goes through step 1; every other datagram on port is a data datagram and goes through step 2. Nothing else is read to decide. The split follows the source and destination checks above and precedes any other processing of the datagram, the packet_id routing of and the replay tracking of included, and that replay tracking MUST NOT move its reordering window, or record a packet_sequence_number as seen, for a datagram that step 1 or 2 has not admitted: such a datagram's packet_sequence_number is an injector's to choose, and one far ahead of the flow's would move the window past the genuine packets, which the receiver would then discard before step 2 could admit them. A record candidate that fails a check of step 1 is dropped as step 1 says; it is never held, hashed as a data datagram or admitted.
A receiver applies the following, in this order, with no variable-length interpretation before a cryptographic check:

li.t: Record datagram (on port, magic "MHM2"). Require 164 <= len <= 1316 and (len - 132) mod 32 == 0. Read the fixed-offset integers magic, kid, epoch, mseq, count, hash_alg and sent and the 32 octets of ctx. Drop before any cryptography if: magic differs; kid is not in the key set, or epoch is outside its range (); (kid, epoch, mseq) is already verified (this drops the second copy of a record with one lookup and one hash, a copy of the previous epoch arriving after its grace period included; a dropped copy whose bytes hash, under the flow's hash_alg, to the digest kept with the verified entry is the record itself and counts as its arrival on this path: it raises the highest_mseq of the path and starts the path's grace period as a verified record would, below, and, where the verified copy arrived on the manifest track and this one is the record's first copy on port (its pairs, kept until then, are released at this arrival;
