a later copy there, the twin or one an injector replays within the retention, counts as a further arrival on the path and measures nothing), the interval between the two arrivals, rounded up to a multiple of manifestTimerMs and capped at the bound of , becomes the mirror's lead if it is the first measured in the stream generation and raises it if it exceeds it, a copy that raises it also handling this record and every record verified on the manifest track within the raised lead before now whose first copy on port has not yet arrived (the verified entry keeps their pairs for this, this record's own bytes carrying its pairs), each pair of such a record as below for a record on port, under the raised lead: a pair marked as having admitted a datagram has its digest recorded as admitted until now + maxAuthDelayMs plus the raised lead; one whose digest is pending has its entry's expiry set to the insertion time plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs plus the raised lead; one whose digest is neither admitted nor pending admits a held datagram or inserts a pending entry with expiry now + maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs plus the raised lead, now being its insertion time; and, once every such record is processed, each datagram held in either hold queue whose digest is now recorded as admitted is dropped (step 2), so that the datagrams of every record the mirror delivered under a lead the receiver had not yet measured, within the bound of , those of the records mirrored while the raising copy was in flight included, are still admitted when they arrive, a late copy of one a pair has admitted is dropped rather than held, and a copy replayed within the retention re-admits nothing a pair has admitted (); a dropped copy whose bytes do not match counts as nothing); epoch is below the current epoch and is not the previous epoch within the grace period this record meets and before the previous epoch's deadline, the bound of plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the current epoch became current (below; a path on which no record of the current epoch has yet been verified, or dropped by the lookup above as its byte-identical copy, has started no grace period, so the previous epoch stays admitted on port until the deadline passes or, once such a record starts that path's period, until that period ends, if sooner, and on the manifest track until the earlier-started of the two paths' periods ends), or, when no record has yet been verified, is below minEpoch or below the pinned floor for its kid; mseq + 64 <= highest_mseq(kid, epoch), the highest_mseq this record meets (below; replay floor, none before a record of that (kid, epoch) has raised a highest_mseq this record meets, no upper bound; the sum does not wrap, ); mseq is above the mseq that closed the epoch, once a verified record has closed it; sent is more than 7 s + maxAuthDelayMs behind, or more than 6 s ahead of, the receiver's UTC clock (freshness: the sender's 1 s bound and the receiver's 5 s bound, plus, behind, the truncation of sent to whole seconds and the delivery of the twin; a receiver that widens its hold per widens the behind tolerance by the same amount for a record read from the manifest track, and not for one on port); count != (len - 132) / 32; hash_alg is not in the receiver's accepted set, or differs from the flow's hash_alg once one is fixed; or, on a receiver that holds the catalog, ctx differs from the value recomputed from it (a receiver without the catalog carries ctx blind, ). The replay floor and the grace period a record meets are its path's: a record on port meets the highest_mseq and the grace period that the records arriving on port, verified or dropped by the lookup above as the record itself, have raised or started; a record read from the manifest track meets the higher of the two paths' highest_mseq values and the earlier-started of their grace periods. The mirror's lead so moves no floor and no grace period a multicast copy meets: a record a relay withholds from the mirror, or one the mirror loses, is tested against the multicast path's own cadence however far the mirror leads, and, while the mirror leads by no more than the bound of , the previous epoch's deadline drops on port only a record of that epoch reordered more than maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs behind the new epoch's first record (), and a mirror that lags the multicast path by the floor brings nothing a receiver still holds. Charge the per-flow verification budget, a token bucket of depth 64 refilled at V tokens per second, V = max(1000, 1.25 x maxBitrate / (8 x 512 x 37)) computed from the flow's declared maxBitrate (), which this profile declares as the endpoint's bandwidth (a record read from the manifest track of charges a second bucket of the same depth and refill, so a record flood on port cannot starve the mirror); drop and count a record that finds it empty (nothing before the signature tells a forged record from a genuine one, so a forged record spends the same token, ). Verify the Ed25519 signature over signed_message; drop on failure, and only on success read first_seq, flags and the digests. If epoch is above the current epoch, or this is the first verified record, make epoch current, record when it became current, and make the former current epoch the previous epoch, with a grace period on each path that ends maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the first record of the new epoch that arrives on it and is verified, or dropped by the lookup above as the record itself (this record starts it on its own path now; port, while no such record has yet arrived there, admits the previous epoch until one starts that path's period and then until that period ends, and the manifest track until the earlier-started of the two periods ends, the sender emitting every twin of it before the new epoch's first record, ; neither path admits it past the previous epoch's deadline, above, which this record sets, so a path on which the new epoch's records are dropped holds the previous epoch open no longer than that), fix the flow's hash_alg from this record if none is fixed yet, and hash every held datagram that has no digest yet; pending entries and held datagrams of the previous epoch are not flushed and live out their expiry. A record of the previous epoch that passes the checks above is processed under that epoch's own floor and verified set and never changes the current epoch. Record (kid, epoch, mseq) as verified, with the time and path of its arrival, its sent and the hash_alg digest of its bytes, and raise the highest_mseq of the path it arrived on. For each (digest, sequence) of the record, in order: if a hold queue holds a datagram with that digest, admit the oldest such datagram, mark the pair as having admitted it, remove it from its queue and record its digest as admitted until now + maxAuthDelayMs plus the mirror's lead (step 2); otherwise insert the pair into the pending table with expiry now + maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs (240 ms at the defaults), plus the mirror's lead, or W on a receiver that applies no lead, for a record read from the manifest track (), an entry so widened keeping its insertion time. Once every pair of the record is processed, drop from both hold queues each datagram still held whose digest is now recorded as admitted: it is a copy of a datagram this record admitted, delivered on the other path or repeated on the same one, which step 2 would not have held after the admission; its drop is not an expiry and counts toward nothing (). If flags bit 0 is set the epoch is closed at this mseq ().

Data datagram (any other datagram on port). Compute D with the flow's hash_alg (a datagram that arrives before the first record of the flow is verified is held without a digest) and look it up in the pending table, which maps a digest to its entries (carousels repeat byte-identical datagrams). Hit: remove the entry lowest in (epoch, sequence) order, admit the datagram, mark the pair of the record that inserted the entry as having admitted it (step 1) and record D as admitted until now + maxAuthDelayMs plus the mirror's lead (). Miss: drop the datagram if D is so recorded (a copy of an admitted datagram delivered again, on any path, is never held); otherwise append (D, datagram) to the hold queue of its path, with expiry now + maxAuthDelayMs + W, each queue bounded to (maxAuthDelayMs + W) x bandwidth / 8000 octets, W being the widening of in milliseconds, zero on the multicast path, and each held datagram counting its payload plus 28 octets on an IPv4 endpoint and 48 on an IPv6 one (its IP and UDP headers on the multicast path), so that empty or short datagrams hold no more entries than those octets pay for; drop the newest on overflow and drop at expiry, so a MoQ unicast path that fills its queue evicts no multicast datagram. Repair symbols follow the same rule, so an injected symbol is dropped before FEC decode. A receiver MUST NOT feed a FEC instance, a keyframe overlay or the packet_id 0 signaling consumer with a datagram of a protected flow that it has not admitted under step 1 or 2, on whatever carrier it arrived (). A FEC instance, a keyframe overlay or the packet_id 0 consumer that has admitted a datagram of a protected flow is a protected consumer, protected under each flow a datagram of which it has admitted (one that a source endpoint and a repair-only endpoint both feed, Section 4, under both), and a symbol admitted under any flow of the multicast object is an admitted symbol in every consumer it reaches: a packet of a track that the endpoint of a flow the consumer is protected under lists, reaching it over any path, a MoQ unicast path included, is a datagram of that flow and is admitted by this step (). A consumer that has admitted none, because the receiver takes the track over MoQ unicast alone while its multicast join completes () or after the failover of , is a MoQ subscriber outside this profile: the MoQ session protects its objects, and it MAY verify them against the records of a manifestTrack (); a consumer protected under one flow of the object is such a subscriber for the tracks of a flow it is not yet protected under, as one that a repair-only endpoint feeds is for a source track the receiver takes over MoQ unicast ( Section 4). On failover a receiver that reads no manifest track discards its protected consumers and continues as such a subscriber; one that does MAY keep them. A receiver holds an endpoint while it is joined to its group, reads its manifestTrack () or receives the broadcast that carries the flow (), and a consumer is protected under a flow only while the receiver holds the flow's endpoint: when the receiver ceases to hold one, on the failover above or on dropping a repair layer ( Section 4), it discards that flow's state as on a streamId change (above) and, since no further record of the flow will arrive, the flow's hold queues with the datagrams they hold, a drop that is no expiry and counts toward nothing; the consumer ceases to be protected under the flow, the symbols it admitted under it staying admitted, and the endpoint's tracks are, for the consumer, unlisted (below) unless another flow it is protected under lists them. At the admission that makes a consumer protected under a flow, the receiver discards every packet of a track that flow's endpoint lists that the consumer still holds and that it did not admit under step 1 or 2, so that none stands, under the deduplication of item 1 of , for the admitted copy of the same symbol; within a protected consumer that deduplication keeps an admitted symbol over an unadmitted one of the same key. For a consumer, a track that no endpoint of a flow it is protected under lists is an unlisted track, one whose symbols reach the consumer only over a MoQ unicast path ( Section 4): a track that no endpoint the receiver holds lists, or one that an endpoint the receiver holds lists while the consumer is not yet protected under that endpoint's flow, its join still completing or its records unread, the multicast copy of such a packet being a datagram of that flow held by this step. A symbol of an unlisted track is not a datagram of any flow the consumer is protected under: it MAY enter a FEC instance under that path's own integrity protection, which vouches for the relay and not for the publisher, neither anchoring nor tripping the fail-closed check of Section 7.3.2, as Section 5.2 provides, and the admission that makes the consumer protected under a flow that lists the track ends this for that track, the discard above dropping each such symbol the consumer still holds and a provisional block those symbols delimited returning its source symbols to the undelimited state of Section 5.4. The rules of this step from here to its end, for blocks, decodes and recovered packets, govern a FEC instance or keyframe overlay only while it is protected under a flow whose endpoint lists its source track. One protected under no such flow, as one that a repair-only endpoint feeds while the receiver takes the source track over MoQ unicast alone ( Section 4), the track unlisted or the join of the endpoint that lists it still completing, is a MoQ subscriber outside this profile for its blocks: the symbols it admitted enter its decodes as admitted symbols, its other packets are what the MoQ session delivers, and Sections 5.4, 9.3 and 9.4 of and Section 6 of govern its blocks as those of a consumer outside this profile, until the admission that makes it protected under a flow whose endpoint lists the track (a record of that flow, from port or its manifestTrack, admitting a source packet under step 1 or this step), at which the discard above applies. Within a protected consumer the block extent such a symbol signals is provisional: a block that only such symbols have delimited yields to an admitted repair packet whose (SS_Start, SSB_length) conflicts with it under Section 5.4, the receiver discarding the provisional block's repair symbols, returning its source symbols to the undelimited state of that section and accepting the admitted packet, so that the first-accepted rule of that section discards an admitted repair packet only for conflict with another admitted one; such a symbol that conflicts with a block an admitted repair packet has delimited is discarded as that section requires. Nor is such a symbol the later signal of Section 9.3 or the packet whose receipt anchors a block's ts there, whether or not an admitted repair packet later delimits the block the symbol delimited (that block's ts is the receipt time of the first packet of it, in the order received, that this profile admits), nor does a block only such symbols have delimited take any SS_ID out of a run or stand as the S_prev of the Group range of Section 7.7: within a protected consumer such a block is held for decoding only, has no ts and no FEC deadline, whatever packets are admitted into or above its range before or after the symbol, and requests no repair, and the SS_IDs in its range that the receiver lacks are, for Section 9.3 and Section 6, runs between the packets the receiver has admitted and the blocks admitted packets have delimited, as if the provisional block were not delimited, each revealed and given its ts only by a packet admitted above it, whether the symbol delimited the block before or after that packet, and classified, requested and cancelled as those sections specify; what the block decodes before such a run's deadline is admitted by its digest, as below, and closes the run or part of it. A relay could otherwise, by one repair packet whose SS_Start lies above what the publisher has sent, give the SS_IDs below it a deadline they reach unrecovered, by one whose range begins at an SS_ID the receiver admitted long ago, delimit a block that takes its ts from that old admission and is past its deadline on arrival, by one whose SSB_length reaches past what the publisher is sending, delimit a block that reaches a deadline before the rest of its range is sent, and force the repair request of Section 6.2 any of those ways, or, by one whose range covers a run that has a ts, take the run's deadline and repair request away, or, by one whose range ends just below a lost SS_ID, narrow the run's Group range to exclude the block that contains it. Under the open-block bound of Section 9.4 the receiver discards a block that has no ts before any block that has a ts, whether or not the track derives an FEC deadline, so that the blocks such symbols delimit, however many a relay sends, evict under a memory cap no block of the multicast path; such a discard gives the block no deadline and no class, forces no repair request, drops the block's repair symbols and returns its source symbols to the undelimited state of Section 5.4. The receiver decodes a block from admitted symbols where they suffice and uses such symbols only for the shortfall. A packet the base instance recovers with such a symbol's help is admitted by its digest like a received datagram, against the pending entries of its window, hashed with the base SS_ID its position in the base block implies (SS_Start + ESI, Section 5.5) appended for the hash only ( Sections 7.1 and 7.2), and on a miss is held in the MoQ unicast path's hold queue, under that queue's expiry and bound, since only such a symbol, which that path alone delivers, made the decode possible, so that its octets and its expiry count toward nothing of the multicast path. A recovered packet that leaves the queue unadmitted, at expiry or on overflow, is not a symbol the receiver holds for Section 6: a block of which the receiver has not admitted every one of its SSB_length source symbols, received or recovered, is unrecovered for that section and for the release below, at its FEC deadline as at any other time, the receiver keeping the packets it admitted (a decode none of whose recovered packets is admitted recovers nothing, a corrupt symbol among those decoded from corrupting what the decode recovers), and it SHOULD discard the symbols of unlisted tracks that fed a decode that left the block unrecovered and decode again when the symbols it then holds suffice, at most once more per block with such symbols' help: a block that two such decodes have left unrecovered takes no further symbol of an unlisted track into a decode, since a relay could otherwise drive one decode of the block per symbol it sends, while a decode from admitted symbols alone, and the admission of a held packet, remain open to it; a held packet admitted after the deadline recovers the block as a received datagram admitted then would, and the receiver SHOULD cancel a repair FETCH then outstanding for it, as Section 6.2 has it for a repair the next RAP makes moot. A packet recovered from admitted symbols alone, by the base instance or a keyframe overlay, is admitted with them; a packet only the overlay recovers with the help of such a symbol has no base SS_ID to hash with ( Section 7.1) and is not delivered. A receiver that can request unicast repair () keeps, instead of letting them expire, the pending entries of each open block that has an FEC deadline: those pending at the admission of the first packet, source or repair, that the receiver admits into the block, and those inserted after it (a mirrored record's entries are inserted up to the lead before the datagrams they cover arrive on the multicast path, and under the bound of until the stream generation has measured a lead, so no span reckoned from the lead in force at the admission names them all; the admitted packet is not necessarily the packet whose receipt set the block's ts in Section 9.3: a datagram held on a miss is admitted, by step 1, after one that a verified record admitted on arrival, and a symbol of an unlisted track no step admits, nor does one set a ts, so a block only such symbols have delimited has no deadline and keeps no entries as a block, the lost SS_IDs in its range keeping theirs as the runs they are, below), until that deadline (the receiver keeps the admission time with the block). A run of lost SS_IDs that the receiver has not delimited () is one such block ( Section 6) of which it holds no packet, and the receiver learns of the run, and of the block's deadline, only from a packet admitted above it ( Sections 5.4 and 9.3; step 2), by when the run's entries would have expired; so for each base instance it also keeps the entries pending at the admission of the source packet of highest SS_ID it has admitted, and those inserted after it (keeping that admission time with the instance; a symbol of an unlisted track, which no step admits, is never this anchor however high its SS_ID) until it admits a source packet of the instance above that SS_ID; a source packet admitted below it moves neither that anchor nor the entries so kept (highest, above and below in SS_ID, and the gap below, under the serial number arithmetic of Section 7.6, so that the anchor follows SS_ID across its wrap to 0). A gap in SS_ID between the two reveals lost SS_IDs, of such a run or of a block that a repair packet alone has delimited ( Section 5.4); each takes the entries so kept as its own from the admission of the source packet of highest SS_ID admitted at or below its lower bounding packet (lower and upper in SS_ID order, Section 6.1; a bounding packet can itself be such a symbol), or of the packet admitted above it where the instance has admitted none below it; otherwise the entries whose expiry has passed by the admission of the packet above are released. The blocks that the admitted repair packets a run's Group range FETCH returns delimit take over the entries so kept; a block that only symbols of an unlisted track the response returns have delimited is provisional as above and takes none, the run keeping its entries, against which the decode of that block admits its recovered packets, until the run is recovered or its requested repair, the FETCH on each layer it needs ( Section 6.2), completes without recovering it, fails or is cancelled. They are block state under the bound of Section 9.4 and are released when the block is recovered, when its deadline passes with no repair requested, when a requested repair, the FETCH on each layer it needs, completes without recovering the block, fails or is cancelled ( Section 6.2), or when the block is discarded under that bound.

section.t: Replay. Receivers in an explicitly configured DVR or replay mode MAY relax the epoch, floor and freshness checks. Clock. The freshness check needs a receiver clock synchronized to UTC within 5 s. A receiver without one MAY skip that check alone; it then accepts any window of the current epoch at join and has no protection against replay of the epoch's earlier windows until its first verified record sets the floor ().

Key rotation. A key change is an epoch change (). The publisher adds the next kid to the catalog with the firstEpoch at which it will sign, at least one catalog lifetime ahead; signs with it from that epoch; and raises minEpoch. A receiver that holds that catalog accepts the retired kid below the successor's firstEpoch only, so records the retired key signs are admitted on port until that path's grace period for the new epoch ends, or while that path has started none, but never past the bound of plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the new epoch became current, and on the manifest track only within the earlier-started of the two paths' periods (step 1 of ); a receiver that verifies no record of the new epoch keeps the epoch before it current, which the retired key still signs, and a receiver whose catalog or pin predates the rotation is exposed to the retired key until it re-fetches or is re-provisioned (). A record with an unknown kid triggers at most one catalog re-fetch per 30 s per receiver; until then such records are dropped. section.name: Broadcast Carriage
section.t: Hybrid receivers that also hold the MoQ catalog verify datagrams of the flow from any path, a MoQ unicast path included, against the same records (); a symbol of an unlisted track, one that no endpoint of a flow the consumer is protected under lists, is not a datagram of any such flow, and what it helps the base instance recover is admitted by digest (). A broadcast carries the flow as an MMTP service ( Section 8.1.2.1; ): the flow's datagrams are the MMTP packets of one MMTP session, carried as the UDP datagrams the sender emits, each the whole MoQ UDP payload, trailer included, on the endpoint's S, G and port, and the records are the sender's record datagrams on the same S, G and port, both copies (), carried in the same IP multicast of the broadcast. A broadcast that re-addresses the flow or its records, or carries the datagrams in any other form, is not covered: the pseudoheader binds S, G and the ports (), and a record verifies as it was signed or not at all. A broadcast-only receiver reads the flow's datagrams and records from the broadcast, forms the pseudoheader and signed_message from the endpoint's S, G, port and streamId, and holds those values and the keys by provisioning (): the SLS of the service describes the MMTP session ( Section 7.2) and nothing of this profile, so streamId and the rest come from provisioning alone, and this document specifies no in-band carriage of them. A record so read is a record on port for step 1 of , as on any multicast path.

section.name: Hash Algorithms
section.t: hash_alg is a Suite ID of the IANA Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry ( Section 9.4), a value from 0 to 63; values 64 to 255 are not Suite IDs and MUST NOT be sent. Only a suite whose output is 256 bits is usable, since every digest field is 32 octets; the truncated suites MUST NOT be used. Suite 1, sha-256 , is mandatory to implement. A receiver MAY implement other 256-bit suites; it drops a record whose hash_alg it does not implement ().

section.name: Catalog as Attack Surface
section.t: The multicast catalog extension directs receivers to join multicast groups and to dial network sources. A hostile or compromised catalog is therefore an attack vector:

li.t: Join amplification: Catalog-directed joins create IGMP/MLD and multicast routing state on intermediate routers (Section 4.1). A catalog listing many endpoints, or rapidly changing endpoints, can exhaust router state or subscribe receivers to unwanted high-bandwidth traffic. Receivers MUST validate that each groupAddress falls within the multicast address ranges given in Section 4.1 before joining, and SHOULD bound the number of concurrent joins performed on behalf of a single catalog.

Attacker-chosen dial-out: The relay field of an AMT network source is an address the receiver dials over UDP. A hostile catalog can direct traffic at arbitrary targets (traffic reflection) or at internal infrastructure (address-space probing). Receivers and relays MUST treat catalog-supplied endpoint and relay addresses as untrusted input and validate them against local policy (such as an allowlist of permitted relays or networks) before dialing, and SHOULD reject loopback, link-local, and otherwise non-routable relay addresses unless explicitly configured.

Resource claims: bandwidth, maxAuthDelayMs and manifestTimerMs size the verification budgets, hold queues and pending table of and, with the manifest track's verification budget, the records verified on that track which a receiver retains for as long as the freshness check of step 1 would pass a copy of them on port, each with the pairs kept until its first copy on port arrives; the widening W of enlarges the unicast path's queue and, on a receiver that applies no lead, the pending expiry of a mirrored record's entries, and the mirror's lead that expiry, the admitted-digest set and the entries kept for unicast repair (step 2, those pending at an admission), both receiver-chosen and capped at 5 s. A receiver bounds all of these by local policy, and the pending entries it keeps for unicast repair by the open-block bound of Section 9.4.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document has no IANA actions. hash_alg values are Suite IDs of the Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry ( Section 9.4), which this document does not change, and the multicast catalog extension (Section 4) requires no registration.

After codec, timescale and groupDurationTicks it carries the entry's FEC instances in ascending instanceId, each as lp16(scheme), u32(sourceSymbols), u32(repairSymbols), u32(symbolSize) and u32(interleaveDepthMs), with no instance count and no instanceId field; an entry without FEC carries lp16("none") and four u32(0) as in -01. scheme is the field -01 named fecAlgorithm, so for an entry with one FEC instance the octets hashed are identical to -01's. One further new sentence and one new clause, each adding no requirement: the fields that params_hash leaves unbound are named as deliberate, and the no-FEC encoding is stated to be distinct from every instance because Section 15.2 reserves "none". The source track of a repair-only endpoint's repair track is the track its source names or the track whose instance names it as repairTrack, in place of depends and fec.repairTrack.

The endpoint auth member manifestPort is removed, and the signed_message prefix of binds u16(port) where it bound u16(manifestPort). In the manifestPort input is dropped, the prefix binds port 5004, and only the signature and the record are regenerated.

also discards, before any parsing or hashing, a datagram on port whose destination address is not G, since endpoints of one S in different groups may share a port; -01 assigned to the flow every datagram on its ports that passed the source check. Step 2 consumes, of the pending entries of a digest, the one lowest in (epoch, sequence) order, where -01 consumed the lowest sequence, which compares unrelated counters when a carousel repeats a datagram across an epoch change.

: both verification budgets, on port and on the manifest track, refill at V = max(1000, 1.25 x maxBitrate / (8 x 512 x 37)) per second from the endpoint's declared bandwidth, instead of at a fixed rate, as states, and holds a sender to the envelope of that bucket, at most 64 + V x t windows in any interval of t seconds; and re-derive the record-flood figures from V, and , and add the budgets to what bandwidth sizes. At V's floor, -01's 1000 verifications per second, the cost paragraph of also corrects -01's figure for a receiver that also reads the manifest track from 0.6 of a core to about 0.86, twice the 0.43 that one bucket's signature checks take, and says that SHA2 instructions speed the hashing, not the signature checks. On a protected endpoint bandwidth is the sender's ceiling for the flow, and a receiver ignores a protected endpoint whose bandwidth is absent or not a positive integer ().

makes the choice leaves to a profile: a receiver clamps a maxAuthDelayMs outside 50 to 1000 to the nearer bound, as that document's browser profile does, and ignores a protected endpoint whose manifestTimerMs is below 1, whose port is not an integer from 1 to 65535 or whose streamId is not an unsigned 32-bit integer; a keys array of no or more than four entries, or one naming a kid or firstEpoch that is not an unsigned 32-bit integer or a publicKey that does not decode to 32 octets, yields no key set at a receiver that takes its keys from the catalog, a receiver that pins keys being unaffected as for a repeated kid or firstEpoch in -01, and a minEpoch that is not an unsigned 32-bit integer admits nothing from the broadcast, as that document requires.

: a receiver admits nothing from a broadcast whose multicast.auth lacks scheme, version, sig or minEpoch, or gives scheme, version or sig a value it does not implement; an absent keys yields no key set; and a receiver ignores a protected endpoint whose streamId is absent or whose senderAddress is absent on an ASM endpoint or present on an SSM endpoint.

Key rotation in : a receiver holds the catalog while its subscription to the catalog track is established, each catalog object that subscription delivers counts as a re-fetch, the catalog lifetime is the bound the publisher assumes on that delivery, and the re-fetch that an unknown kid triggers is a REQUEST_UPDATE on that subscription with FILL_PARAMETERS.

Step 2 of counts each held datagram's IP and UDP headers, 28 or 48 octets, against its hold queue's bound as well as its payload. The publisher keeps every endpoint of the multicast object at one epoch, and keeps within the old bandwidth, maxAuthDelayMs or manifestTimerMs for one catalog lifetime after publishing a new one (); a change of a value that ctx binds interrupts the flow at each receiver until its catalog and the records agree (); a sender sets flags bit 0 on the record of the last window of an epoch whose end it plans (). bounds the age of a window admitted at join by 13 s + maxAuthDelayMs within the clock bounds, plus W on a receiver that widens its tolerance, where -01 gave the freshness tolerance on sent, 7 s + maxAuthDelayMs, as that age, and W alone on such a receiver.

adds that an injection that reaches a replication point can move every receiver below it that holds a MoQ session onto MoQ unicast at once, by failover or, for the blocks it leaves unrecovered, by the repair of , an amplification of the kind that Section 2.1 warns of, driven by the loss the injector causes rather than by an injected datagram that invalidates an object, and that a publisher that offers the fallback sizes it, or bounds what its relays admit, for that. It adds that one record with an unknown kid, which needs no key, makes every receiver below that point that holds the catalog re-fetch the catalog at once, a burst on the relays that can recur every 30 s, and the cost paragraph of counts that re-fetch. It also corrects the residual that a key pin leaves: a lowered minEpoch admits records of an earlier epoch signed with a still-listed kid at any later join as well, those of the highest epoch verified under that kid and of every later epoch in its range, where -01 named a receiver's first join under a kid only. The floor a key pin keeps is now one for each broadcast whose keys the receiver pins, shared only by that broadcast's flows, where -01 kept one per receiver for all its flows. It scopes the detection of deletion, loss and reordering to an epoch of a flow, since sequence and mseq restart at an epoch change, where -01 claimed it within a flow.

names , a new informative reference, as the format it restates by value. Step 1 of writes the replay floor as mseq + 64 <= highest_mseq(kid, epoch), a sum that does not wrap, in place of -01's subtraction, which underflows while highest_mseq is below 64, and states that mseq increases by one per window, as in and as the replay floor and the twin deadline assume, and that neither counter wraps within an epoch. In the twin goes on its own at the maxAuthDelayMs / 2 deadline when window mseq + 2 has not closed by then, where -01 said opened.
: flags bit 0 is the least significant bit of the octet (mask 0x01), as in ; -01 did not say which end of the octet bit 0 is.

New : a sender SHOULD set ECT(0) on the data datagrams and manifest records of a protected flow, a receiver that can read the ECN field MUST treat a CE-marked datagram, on a protected flow only a data datagram it admits or a record it verifies, as a lost one in endpoint selection and in the failover to MoQ unicast and in no other reaction to loss, never toward adding or holding repair, and an AMT gateway MUST carry the ECN field through decapsulation per as Section 6.1.4 applies it to AMT, a section that recommends the same support in a relay without requiring it; points to it. , and are new normative references, and a new informative one.

: params_hash and ctx are unchanged from -01: the example's entry has one FEC instance, which the -02 layout of hashes to the same octets. In the listed inputs the label fecAlgorithm is renamed scheme.
: the keyframe overlay in item 1 now cites .
Sections 4 and 4.1: the catalog envelope and the mmtp packaging value are now cited by section of at its -02 numbering.

Editorial: every heading carries an explicit anchor; no existing anchor changes. The change log is now one appendix with a subsection per revision, as in . The catalog example of shows the public key of , base64url-encoded, in place of a placeholder, and declares the maxBitrate of the well-known example, which describes the same flow, as its bandwidth: 8000000 in place of 100000000. The Abstract no longer says that MoQ carries MMTP packets on QUIC datagrams, and it says that the signed manifest records travel in band.

Section 1: added a paragraph on TreeDN as an incremental path to native multicast, with AMT relays serving unicast-only networks; receivers without UDP socket access stay on MoQ unicast. The statement that MoQ relays MAY operate as TreeDN nodes is removed, because defines no such role. The catalog extension is no longer called container-agnostic.
Section 1.1: a catalog-provided service name or relay address is a discovery input, not proof that an upstream is reachable or healthy.
Section 2: defines service hostname and protocol health.
Sections 3 and 4.1: the availability of several transports, the preference for SFN diversity reception, and the configurability of hysteresis thresholds are no longer stated with BCP 14 keywords.

New Section 3.1: a receiver given a service hostname for a MoQ upstream or an AMT relay resolves it at connection time and treats the A and AAAA answers as candidates. It selects a candidate only after protocol health: MoQ session setup and the capability check for a MoQ upstream, or the AMT exchange and the first data or a bounded wait for an AMT relay. It races a bounded batch, cancels the losers, honors DNS TTLs, and does not pin an address across reconnects.

Section 4.1: an endpoint lists only mmtp tracks and the fec-repair tracks that repair them, and a receiver ignores an endpoint that lists any other track. A loc or cmaf track reaches multicast through an mmtp rendition track in its altGroup.

Section 4.1: an endpoint names tracks in the namespace of the catalog track. The IPv6 ASM range is now ff00::/8 outside the SSM range ff3x::/32, which admits transient, unicast-prefix-based and embedded-RP groups. IGMPv3 and MLDv2 are cited to and , which obsolete RFC 3376 and RFC 3810.
Section 4.1: points to Section 6.3, under which a receiver SHOULD pause or end the unicast subscriptions that the multicast path replaces once multicast delivery is verified.

Section 4.2.1: the new discovery value "dns" resolves the relay service hostname to candidates that the subscriber validates (Section 3.1). It is now the recommended method when a relay service hostname is available, in place of "driad". relay is a hostname with "dns", a literal address with "manual", and absent with "driad". A losing AMT candidate sends a Membership Update with the leave before its socket closes. The search starts with a relay in the subscriber's own network, found with DNS-SD or the AMT anycast addresses ( Section 3.1.2). The claim that DRIAD relay addresses are typically anycast is removed. The examples name a relay service hostname. The port field now says that a value other than 2268 departs from and never applies to a relay found by DRIAD.
Section 4.2.2: the atsc3 fields cite and , and slsUri acquires the SLS of an MMTP service, its MP table included ( Section 7.2), in place of the S-TSID with FEC parameters of -00.

Section 5: the paragraph on LOC and CMAF objects now refers to the mmtp rendition rule of Section 4.1. It no longer says that multicast carriage uses MMTP "regardless of a track's unicast packaging". The catalog-derived FEC configuration now also covers the Reed-Solomon parameters ( Section 4.5). The transport table drops the QUIC datagram row, because Section 4.3 sends the objects of an mmtp track only in subgroups. The mapping of MMTP packets onto Multicast QUIC DATAGRAM frames, and the use of on that channel, are now described, informatively, in Section 11.3, which that document's -01 makes informative, rather than specified there.

Section 6: failover uses the joins of Section 3.5 (LOCATION_FILTER Next Object or Relative Start, and FILL_PARAMETERS for the current group). These replace the "Largest Object filter" and "Next Group Start filter", which that document no longer defines. A paused unicast subscription is resumed instead of subscribing again.

Section 6.2: "standalone FETCH" is now FETCH, and "Largest Location" is now Largest Object, with the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter cited. The text now says that repair Group IDs use only [0, 2^62) of the MoQ Transport Group ID range, which goes up to 2^64 - 1. A relay that does not hold a repair-track group fetches it upstream, so a FETCH fails only when no publisher upstream still holds the group.

New Section 6.3: after a switch to multicast, a receiver SHOULD pause its unicast subscriptions with REQUEST_UPDATE (FORWARD 0) or end them with STOP_SENDING, and resumes paused ones on failover. It keeps any repair layer that no endpoint carries and that it combines with multicast source symbols.

Editorial: the Abstract and Section 1 expand MMTP, AMT and DRIAD. Section 1 no longer calls failover seamless, Section 1.1 calls multicast an additional delivery path instead of an optimized one, and Section 3 calls MoQ/WebTransport the fallback that every client supports instead of the universal fallback. The examples of Section 4.1 use a documentation address.
References: and now name their -01 revisions. ATSC A/331, ATSC A/322, ARIB STD-B60 and FIPS 180-4 are now cited; BLAKE3 is no longer cited.
replaces bc-provenance version 1 with version 2; the BCPV1 manifest_object, its "BCPV1-sig" prefix, the compaction member, the Merkle Tree Hash and the 198-octet test vector are withdrawn.
The digest is hash-agile: hash_alg is a Named Information Suite ID () and sha-256 is the only mandatory algorithm. The keyed authScope is removed (S, G, the ports and streamId separate domains).
Receivers that implement the profile enforce it; the "shadow" and "off" modes and the enforcement member are removed.

The catalog auth object gains a REQUIRED version member, 2 (); keys, each entry with a firstEpoch, replaces publicKey, keyId and previousKey; minEpoch is added; hash, compaction and the tracks array (mediaTrack, authScope, sourceSymbolFormat) are removed. A protected endpoint carries an auth object of its own: manifestPort, streamId, senderAddress, maxAuthDelayMs, manifestTimerMs, and manifestTrack, which moves there from the tracks entry and becomes OPTIONAL.
A multicast object that carries auth requires auth on every endpoint ().

A packet of a track the endpoint lists is a datagram of the flow on every path that delivers it to a consumer protected under the flow, one that has admitted a datagram of it, a MoQ unicast path included, and is verified against the same records, a consumer that several endpoints feed being protected under each and a symbol admitted under any flow of the object being admitted in it, a consumer being protected under a flow only while the receiver holds its endpoint, joined to its group, reading its manifestTrack or receiving the broadcast that carries the flow, and leaving one discarding that flow's state and hold queues, ending the protection under it and keeping what was admitted; only a symbol of an unlisted track, one that no endpoint of a flow the consumer is protected under lists, a held endpoint's track the consumer is not yet protected under included until the admission that makes it so, and that a MoQ unicast path alone therefore delivers to it, is outside every such flow and MAY enter a FEC instance under that path's own protection, a block that only such symbols have delimited yielding to an admitted repair packet that conflicts with it; the block rules of step 2 govern a FEC instance or keyframe overlay only while it is protected under a flow whose endpoint lists its source track, one protected under no such flow, as one a repair-only endpoint feeds while the source track comes over MoQ unicast alone, being a MoQ subscriber outside the profile for its blocks until a record of a flow that lists the track admits a source packet. A packet recovered from admitted symbols alone is admitted with them, the receiver decoding from admitted symbols where they suffice; a packet the base instance recovers with such a symbol's help is admitted by its digest, hashed with the base SS_ID its block position implies, a miss held in the MoQ unicast path's hold queue, and a block is recovered only once every one of its source symbols is admitted, a recovered packet dropped unadmitted at expiry or on overflow leaving it unrecovered, the receiver then SHOULD discard the unlisted-track symbols that fed the decode and decode again when what it holds suffices, at most once more per block with such symbols' help, and a held packet admitted after the FEC deadline recovers the block, the receiver then SHOULD cancel a repair FETCH outstanding for it; a packet only the overlay recovers with such help is not delivered, and a symbol of an unlisted track gives no block or run its ts or FEC deadline and neither anchors nor trips the fail-closed check of Section 6.3.9, a block only such symbols delimit being decoded only, with no ts and no deadline, the lost SS_IDs in its range staying runs that a packet admitted above them reveals, and a block with no ts being discarded under the open-block bound before any block that has a ts. A copy of an admitted datagram delivered again is never held, whether step 1 or step 2 admitted it. At the admission that makes a consumer protected under a flow it discards what it holds, unadmitted, of the tracks that flow's endpoint lists, and its deduplication keeps an admitted symbol over an unadmitted one. A track taken over MoQ unicast alone, before the multicast join completes or after failover, is a MoQ subscription outside the profile unless the receiver verifies it against the records of a manifestTrack (, ).

A receiver that can request unicast repair keeps the pending entries of an open block with an FEC deadline and, since a run of lost SS_IDs is revealed only by a packet admitted above it, those pending at the admission of the source packet of highest SS_ID each base instance has admitted and those inserted after it, as block state under the bound of Section 9; step 1 drops the other held copy of a datagram it admits, which counts toward nothing; a record meets a 64-deep replay floor per (kid, epoch), and a record of the previous epoch is admitted within a grace period of maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs, in place of the previousKey overlap of -00, floor and grace period kept per arrival path (manifestPort, the manifest track), the floor raised by the records arriving on the path, verified or dropped as the byte-identical copy of a verified one, the period ending that long after the first such record of the new epoch on the path, manifestPort admitting the previous epoch while that path has started none, a record read from the mirror meeting the higher of the two floors and the earlier-started period, and no record of the previous epoch admitted past the bound of plus maxAuthDelayMs + 2 x manifestTimerMs after the new epoch became current; the sender transmits each record twice, the byte-identical twin after the last datagram the record covers, no later than maxAuthDelayMs / 2 after the record and before the signed record of window mseq + 64, so that it arrives above the floor; a generation reset discards every per-flow item but the budgets and the hold queues; the hold queues are per path, so a MoQ unicast path that fills its own evicts nothing from the multicast path's, and only the multicast path's expiries and the manifestPort bucket's drops count toward failover; a unicast receiver widens its hold, its hold queue with it, and the freshness tolerance of the records it reads from the manifest track, by at most 5 s, a record on manifestPort keeping the unwidened tolerance, one that reads the mirror and will not join the multicast path widening the pending expiry of a mirrored record's entries by the same W, and a receiver reading the mirror that has joined or may yet join widens the pending expiry of a mirrored record's entries and the life of its admitted digests by the mirror's lead, a per-flow value it measures, the bound until the generation's first measurement (, , ).
A keys array that repeats a kid or a firstEpoch yields no key set: the receiver admits nothing from the broadcast ().

Per-flow receiver state belongs to the stream generation: a change of the endpoint's streamId discards it, the budgets and the hold queues excepted, and the next record is processed as the first of the flow; the current epoch is kept with the kid that set it, and a re-fetch or re-provisioning after which that (kid, epoch) fails the range check of resets the flow the same way ().

A broadcast carries the flow as an MMTP service: the flow's datagrams as the MMTP packets of one MMTP session, carried as the sender's UDP datagrams on S, G and port, and the records as the sender's record datagrams on manifestPort, a broadcast that re-addresses either flow or carries the datagrams in any other form being uncovered. This document no longer covers ROUTE: the carriage of -00, the record in the ROUTE signaling carousel and the signed group digest in an ALC/LCT EXT_AUTH header, is removed, the profile having no inclusion proofs, and so is the sourceSymbolFormat member of -00, whose only value named the authenticated bytes of that revision, trailer excluded ().

defines S for the tuple rule (sourceAddress on an SSM endpoint, auth.senderAddress on a protected ASM endpoint, absent on an unprotected ASM endpoint), binds each (S, G, port) tuple to at most one endpoint object as well as one namespace, adds the same rule for a protected endpoint's (S, G, manifestPort) tuple, and requires a track listed on an endpoint to carry the catalog track's namespace ( Section 5.2.2); a receiver ignores an endpoint that lists another.

no longer delegates source trust to the AMT relay: an ASM receiver, and a receiver reached through an AMT gateway on SSM, discards a datagram whose IP source address is not the endpoint's sender before parsing or hashing it ().
